en: One day, while I was sorting through a disordered collection of writings, I came across several folios of a *yulu* (recorded sayings).

They were moth-eaten and only partially preserved—sometimes three or five lines, sometimes a hundred or so characters. Yet they were seasoned with maturity, direct and spirited, daring, eccentric, and extraordinary.

Whether speaking truth or employing deception, every sentence struck the mark. I was struck with awe; however, as the beginning and end were ruined and decayed, I did not know who this person was. I sought them out...
Bashan obtained a complete copy; it was originally composed by the Fifth Patriarch, Yuan. Yet Yuanwu and Huqiu have now brought it out from this very source.

Only then can one believe that the treasures of the Persians are distinct, and that such matters exist in the world. Suddenly, a monk in black robes arrived at my door, holding this scroll and requesting a preface.
Having read it several times, [I see] lightning and sparks flashing and flickering; it is both *amṛta* (clarified butter) and poison, its colors—

The colors were present together; he stood there with such solemnity that it was as if one were seeing the personal bearing of a former acquaintance. Only then did he realize the significance of the name "Bridge-Breaker" (Duànqiáo);

indeed, it was not obtained in vain. With palms joined, he offered praise and acted as a witness for him. Nevertheless, those who recognize a true man are few, while those who merely follow the sound are many.
For now, let this collection remain anonymous so that those throughout the various regions with the "eye of discernment" may try to guess the master's identity. The master’s name is Miaolún. Tian.
A person of Tai. On the first day of the first month of the first year of the Xianchun era. Preface by Lin Xiyi of Yanzhai.

Preface by Lin Xiyi.

The Discourse Record of Master Duanyue (Bridge-Breaker) upon his Initial Residence at Zhiyuan Chan Temple on Mount Ruifeng in Taizhou, compiled by Attendant Wenbao and Shanjing.
On the eleventh day of the third month in the first year of the Chunyou era, the Master entered the monastery. Pointing to the Main Gate, he said: "The Great Way has no..."
The Gate. Where do you all intend to enter? He then lifted his foot and said, "Look underfoot.
The Buddha Hall. Two thousand years ago, I was not your equal; two thousand years hence, you shall not be my equal.
Holding up the incense, he said, "Look, look! I shall give you a fire at the cold spot."
He sits in his room, spanning one zhang across and ten chi vertically. Even a monk with clear vision cannot approach him.
If there were someone who could turn their body and release their breath right here, even the waters of Jetavana would not yet be yours to drink.
Holding up the notice: it pierces the nostrils of men and exchanges their eyes. It all comes down to this one sentence alone.
How can you see it? The title is clear.
He held up the Dharma robe. "This single piece of ox-hide has entirely enveloped all the old monks of the world.
Today, New Jiyuan was slightly late in avoiding it and has likewise suffered its harm;
there is no choice but to joyfully accept it, wear it upon one's head, and don it upon one's back—how could one fear getting muddy?"
Pointing to the Dharma-seat, he said: "The entire earth is this King of Jewel Flower Throne.

It is only because you people are unable to tread upon it that you cause the Jeta Grove to take up patterns and sketches here, speaking of the east and pointing to the west. Where there is no staircase, you erect a staircase.
He ascended the seat, took up the incense, and offered a prayer.

The ritual for the Venerable Patriarchs is concluded. Next, he holds up the incense and says: "This incense was once picked up from a heap of discarded papers when I was traveling on pilgrimage to Yunju in years past.
Without reason, it has brought me here to the head of the Thousand-Fathom Cliff, where I have run into one who cannot be roasted nor boiled."

As soon as he was sniffed by it, his breath ceased entirely. He burned it in the incense burner as an offering to the Living Buddha, Chan Master Wuzhun Daokai, Abbot of Xingsheng Wanshou Chan Temple on Mount Jing, to repay the kindness of the Dharma-milk.

He then sat cross-legged (the questions and answers are not recorded). He then said: "Śākyamuni has already passed away; Maitreya has not yet been born. Today is precisely the time for the new [Buddha]."
The Master of Jetavana, Zhangzi, appeared in the world to preach the Dharma; he did not engage in long-winded or abbreviated speech, nor in crooked or straightforward discourse.
Relying solely upon his own bare, fundamental ground, he brought forth a single phrase to cause those in heaven and among men who had not yet heard to hear, and those who had not yet seen to see.
He then took up his staff and said: "Even if Master Luk, the founder of this mountain, were to come forth, he would have to stroke [this staff]..."
Zheng laughed heartily and said, "Since I departed three hundred years ago, I have never heard such news.
Nevertheless, even though it is so, how can one help it that the staff has not yet nodded its head? Why is this? The Ten-Thousand-Year Pine stands atop Mount Zhurong.
He then raised another case: When Baoshou opened the hall for the first time, Sansheng pushed forward a monk; Baoshou struck him immediately.
The Holy One said: "To act as a teacher in such a manner not only blinds this monk’s eyes, but it will blind the eyes of the entire city of Zhenzhou.
Shou then returned to his quarters. The Master [Zhaozhou] commented: "Of these two great elders, one has the head of a deer and the eyes of a rat;
the other has the tail of a scorpion and the heart of a wolf. Yet they both cause this monk to meet a bare fist with a white staff—this is truly senseless!"
"End. Although it is thus, if one were not led by the fisherman, how could one have seen the waves?
That evening there was a small-scale sermon (*kōan*): "Deshan’s small-scale sermon was 'not answering questions'—this is a traitor in a time of peace.

Zhaozhou’s small-scale sermon, however, was 'answering questions'—this is a hero in a time of chaos. These two old fellows each have a transgression as vast as the heavens. [Then] the new Jiyuan entered the monastery.

The matters are many; I have not yet had the leisure to verify them. Tonight, I shall first lend a hand to my ancestral father to mend this broken sand-pot, so that all people may together enjoy its use.
[He strikes a circular shape with his whisk. Do you understand? The Southern Dipper turns westward.
The Big Dipper shifts eastward; [the Master] rises again. A monk asks Touzi, "What is the Ten-Body Tamer? Touzi descends from his meditation seat and stands there. The Master composes a verse:
The dawn flowers first break, their dewy fragrance fresh; Alone in the empty mountains, they are coldly set against the clouds. Suddenly struck by spring...
A light breeze touches them; the pale red petals fall in scattered profusion.

The Administrative Head (Zhishi) ascends the hall: Amidst the flowers, butterflies dance; upon the willows, orioles sing. Even Gautama was not yet enlightened; even Bodhidharma still remained deluded.
Entrust this to those in the monastic community who are capable of great deeds: When the moment arises, each and every one must be clearly grasped. Suddenly, when grasped—*not*... [text breaks off]
[The monk] said, "I have attained it. [The Master] remarked, "Your calculation is incorrect. The old monk of Jeta Grove, however, will speak with you in three parts.
He ascended the hall and cited the case where Ānanda asked Kāśyapa, "Aside from the golden robe bestowed by the World-Honored One, what else was secretly transmitted?
Kāśyapa called out, "Ānanda! Ānanda responded. Kāśyapa said, "Throw down the banner-pole in front of the gate!"
The Master’s verse says: "The family style of our indolence is known to both; We rely on each other for coarse tea and plain rice.
In the end, it is difficult for brothers to live together; There is no avoiding that we must go our separate ways."

Ascending the hall for the Buddha-Bathing ceremony: On the eighth day of the fourth month, Siddhārtha was born; heaven and earth were filled with clamor and noise. Old Shao-yang wanted to beat them to death.
But how does this compare to Jeta Grove, where water is scooped up and poured over the head? A-he-he! Though it be a dead snake, if one knows how to handle it, it comes alive.
A Small Sermon for the Summer Retreat: Zen, Zen! Severing the connecting ropes, piercing left and right. Dao, Dao! Producing brooms, sweeping horizontally and vertically.
A clever fellow who understands this directly can then observe the summer retreat within the cauldrons and furnace coals, and protect life amidst the sword-trees and knife-mountains.
The heavenly demons will have no way to spy upon him; the Buddhas and Patriarchs will have cause to praise him. If it is not so—

Within these ninety days, throughout the twelve periods of the day and night, he has done nothing but walk by the mountains and along the water’s edge; he has done nothing but sit upon rocks and at the roots of pines.
It is simply that when he encounters people hereafter, he must not say that he spent the summer retreat at Jetavana. Why?
Because it is but a day’s journey from here to Huangyan. Again, he cited the case where King Liang asked Bodhidharma, “What is the First Noble Truth?”
One meaning. Huineng said, "Vast and empty—there is no sage. The King asked, "Who is it that stands before me? Huineng said, "I do not know. The Master [Zhaozhou] commented:
"The old barbarian came from the Western Heaven carrying a wooden nut, and he has traded away people's eyes for nothing.
Had it not been for the King of Liang, he would have nearly met a deadly hand. Nevertheless, everyone must look out for themselves. After a long silence, he said, "Attentive!"
It is understood. Ascending the hall, he said: "The heavens are naturally high; the earth is naturally thick. Each and every one is not 'one'; even 'three times three' is not 'nine.
Only the old master Da’eng of Mount Budu loved it: when seeing someone, he would bow deeply and hold his hands high. Does this have anything to do with the Buddha-dharma?"
In principle, there is none. *Tut!* Shut that foul mouth!
Entering the hall for the summer retreat in Central China: the first half of the summer has already passed; new matters have not been added.
The second half of the summer has not yet arrived; old matters have not diminished. Now, as for both the new and the old, set them aside. You people, tell me: what is this matter?
After a long silence, he said: "The nights are short and sleep is insufficient; the days are long and hunger remains in abundance.
This was the Small *Prasāda* (Small *Cana*) for the end of the summer retreat. One plowshare of fallow land, one basket of seeds sown—Daiō left much in a state of disorder.
One meal at midday, one sleep after nightfall—Dàomèi’s failures were even more numerous. Although this summer at Jetavana has been quiet and desolate...

Utterly desolate and stark. In the kitchen, there is not even a grain of rice to attract flies; in the bag, there is not a single thread to bind ants. Yet, for now, I shall not beat this drum or blow this flute.
Who else cares whether you have knots to untie or no knots to tie? Seven or eight people point at a horse and call it a donkey;
three or four people take a tortoise and certify it as a turtle. Truly remarkable! To forge a sword, one must use the iron of Bīnzhou.

The Master struck the meditation seat once. He then raised the case again: Dongshan addressed the assembly, saying, "At the end of summer and the beginning of autumn, brothers, whether you go east or west, you must head toward a place ten thousand *li* away where there is not a single blade of grass.
But as for that place ten thousand *li* away where there is not a single blade of grass—how does one go there?
Later, a monk cited this to Shishuang, who said, "As soon as you step out the door, it is already grass. Dongshan...
Shan said, "In the land of the Great Tang, how many people could there possibly be? The Master picked up [the staff] and said, "These two venerable elders—one has a ten-fold barrier upon his tongue;
the other has a three-colored thread beneath his feet. If you can examine them thoroughly, I shall give you a pair of straw sandals."
Ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat, he opened his cloth bag and picked up his staff, saying, "To leave is up to you; to stay is also up to you.
As for that single phrase that penetrates all quarters, Jeta Grove has spoken it to you. He then shook his hand and said, "Not yet! Not yet!"

Ascending the hall on the Mid-Autumn Festival, [the Master said: "At Vulture Peak they spoke of the moon; at Caoxi they pointed to the moon. Examining this closely, it amounts to nothing more than half a wedge.
But here in Jetavana, not sparing a single hair of his eyebrows, he reveals it clearly and directly. Raising his whisk, he said: "Round and full, it leaves the coastal mountains.
Raising the whisk again, he said: "Gradually it emerges from the path of the clouds. Drawing a circle, he said: "This night, the single orb is full."
He threw down [his staff] and said, "Where is pure light not present? He gave a shout and then descended from his seat.
On the occasion of the Summer Retreat, he ascended the hall and said: "Today at Jetavana, we enter the summer retreat. I have nothing to offer you all.
However, having returned yesterday from the county seat, I have a turning phrase to present to the great assembly. He then said: "Outside the Yan-zhan Quarter, a pair of straw sandals."
"I shall certainly sell it for seven coins.
He ascends the hall and says, "All minds are the Buddha-mind," and then he shouts, "This, however, is not the Buddha-mind.
All dharmas are the Buddha-dharma," and he raises his staff, saying, "This, however, is not the Buddha-dharma. Since this is not the Buddha-mind...
"It is not the Buddha-dharma. Ultimately, what is it? [The Master] threw down his staff and said, "A-la-la! A-la-la! Small Retreat Assembly *Xiaochan*:
On the fifteenth day of the fourth month, one’s head touches heaven and one’s feet tread upon the earth. On the fifteenth day of the seventh month...
Feet treading the earth, head touching the heavens—exhausting its binding, it is utterly unobtainable; investigating its release, it is utterly unobtainable.
That which is unobtainable is itself utterly unobtainable. If you people can cast even half an eye toward this point, you will understand.
"The Yellow-Faced Old Man calls for his shoe-cleaner; the Blue-Eyed Barbarian summons his foot-washer.
As for all other understandings like mosquitoes and gnats, or abilities like ants and termites—stay outside the gate!
If you continue to dally from today until the third or fourth day, drifting aimlessly and muddled in confusion—HŪṂ! Return to me the ninety days' worth of meal-money! Again, he cites Xiangyan:
He addressed the assembly, saying: "It is like a man climbing a tree, with a branch in his mouth, his feet not treading on branches, and his hands not grasping branches.
Suddenly someone asks him, 'What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? If he answers him, he loses his body and life; if he does not answer, he violates the questioner's inquiry.
At that time, the Senior Monk Tuhou stepped forward and said, "I do not ask about being on the tree; tell me what you have to say while under the tree."
"Come with a single phrase. Yan Sui laughed heartily. The Master remarked: "Xiangyan has spread a net to encompass all the monks under heaven.
Although Head Upadhyaya Hu was outside the net when he met him, alas, he still ended up falling inside it."
Ascending the hall: The ninety days of this summer retreat have now come to an end. When Hanshan meets Shide, they hold hands to discuss the origins [of their meeting].
But tell me, what do they speak of? Pears come from Qingzhou; dates come from Zhengzhou.

Xie Daoniu ascends the hall to bid farewell to his old associates. He cites Master Ciming’s ascent of the hall, which says: "The winds rustle in the cool scenery; Companions visit this desolate place.
Tea is brewed with water from below the mountain; The cauldron is heated by firewood from within the cave.

Master Ciming, though he opened wide the eastern gate to attend to his noble guests, when scrutinized, cannot avoid using the monastery’s communal property for private purposes. How does he compare to Jītuān (Jetavana)? [He does not.]
When a guest arrives, simply abide in the present moment. But what is the principle of abiding in the present? After a long silence, he said:
"Face to face, heart to heart; if human relations are good, even drinking water will nourish you."
Ascending the hall for the Bathing of the Buddha ceremony: When Śākyamuni was first born, he was fortunately pure and clean.

Yet, for no reason, his descendants of later generations vied with one another to splash foul water over his head, claiming they were repaying his virtue and requiting his kindness. Little did they know that they were instead adding a layer of filth to his body.
Since I, a descendant of the Jetavana Grove, have the misfortune of being among the last of his lineage, I cannot help but perform a different ritual. [He picks up the whisk.]
With a ladle with a broken handle, he scoops up water without getting his hands wet;

he bathes his formless body, penetrating directly from top to bottom, so that there is joy and exhilaration—not only for my Buddha, but for all sentient beings throughout the great earth, who are simultaneously filled with joy;
even the staff itself is joyful, whereupon he throws it down and says, "Joyful! Joyful!"
Small Sermon for the Summer Retreat: "This very mind is Buddha"—a tortoise rolls a golden ball through fire.
"Neither Buddha nor mind"—a blue hare hangs a precious mirror in the water. This summer at Jetavana, we shall thus open the examination hall and set forth the topics.
If you people can, within these ninety days, without raising a hand, reveal a single principle; without moving a tongue, utter a single word—then it is settled.

Take the heart-emptiness as your degree and become a crown prince among Chan masters. If you seek to know through thought or resolve through deliberation—seeking the intended meaning before words or clarifying the source within a phrase—not only will you fail the sages of old, but you will also bury your own self.
Hearing this announcement, is there anyone among the assembly who can stride alone across the crimson heavens? Come forth, overturn the meditation seat, and shout the great assembly into dispersal!
Zhongdimu: "If you are not one of the Dragon Gate guests, take care not to suffer a black mark on your forehead. Again, he raised the "Wild Fox" kōan and offered this verse:
"The sand gulls play all day by the river's edge; Time and again they float up, time and again they sink. A single blast from the fisherman’s flute startles them away;
Yet they fly back down once more into the heart of the blue waves."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "How many clumsy oxen are there? They are all spending the summer retreat at Rui Peak. Some have the intent to lie amidst the moon and sleep among the clouds;

others have no such intent and instead pull the plow and drag the yoke. East of the stream and west of the stream, atop the ridges and below the ridges, they drink water and drink water, eat grass and eat grass.
But first and foremost, you must not trespass upon the crops. He struck the meditation seat and descended from it.
Small-scale *chanshi* (private instruction) for the end of the summer retreat, also expressing thanks to Head Seat Yi. The mountain stream flows coolly; the cliff clouds drift in layers.

Filling the ears, nothing is heard; filling the eyes, nothing is seen. In his early years of traveling the path, Zhuanmen [Ananda] journeyed throughout twenty-three provinces and forty-seven counties.
Gathering these fragments together, he packed them into a single bag. When he picked it up, it was as perilous as a precipice; when he set it down, it was as level as the earth.
A mirror surface. A horse’s winnowing basket knows it instantly. He comes running and leaps forward to take a look—*pang*. You, you stagnant wares!
Though not worth a single coin, you are remarkably efficacious. Why do you not open yourself on the day of *svairacārya* (self-indulgence) and distribute yourself equally as alms?
"I would simply make the poor and lowly wealthy and noble, and the wealthy and noble poor and lowly. The mountain monk was pierced through by this;

unconsciously, his hands and feet grew restless, and his heart and gallbladder trembled. He struck the *zhuzhang* (monk’s staff) and said: "Through the iron wall and silver mountains, a single thread passes. He then raised the case again.
A monk asked Master Fengxue, "The summer retreat is over; we request that you, Master, offer words of commendation for our labor.
Fengxue said, "Before I have even had time to pick up a handful of fragrant grass, the six-ringed golden staff rings out, shaking the void. The Master (Zhaozhou) commented:

"To 'cut water and trim clouds,' to 'carve ice and engrave jade'—Fengxue was certainly not lacking in these skills. Yet, alas, he failed to grasp the immediate occasion. Had Jeta Grove seen him at that moment..."
When asked in such a manner, he immediately struck him with a staff. Why? Because to see what is right and not act upon it is a lack of courage.
On the fifth day of the first lunar month, during the Festival of the Sages, he ascended the hall and said: "This is my [birthday]."
On this day of the Emperor’s auspicious birthday, the subjects of the Jetavana Garden take up the Mount Sumeru mallet and strike the drum of empty space.

They assemble Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges to expound immeasurable Dharma gates, thereby celebrating His ten-thousand-year longevity. Nevertheless—[the Master] raises his whisk and says:
Now tell me: by which Buddha was this Dharma-gate spoken? [The Master] threw his whisk behind him and descended from the seat.
Having retired from the monastery, he ascended the hall; having come to reside at Rui-feng, he went to reside at Rui-yan. Before playing the "Snow Song," let us first speak our local dialect.
Striking the meditation seat, he said: "Do you understand? Thirteen [turns] between heaven and earth.
Compiled by the Attendant for the Recorded Sayings of Master Duanqiao upon his relocation to Jingtu Chan Temple at Ruiyan in Taizhou.
He entered the monastery and pointed to the triple gate, saying: "In years past, when I went out through this gate, at every step I trod upon it;
today, as I enter through this gate, at every turn I collide with it. Ultimately, by what means shall one verify this? He then looked up at the monastery’s nameplate and said:
"It is truly fitting to say so."
The Buddha Hall. [口@力]. It has been a long time since we have seen one another. He then bows and says, "Ten thousand blessings to you, Gautama.
He sits within the room; he does not let anyone out from within, nor does he let anyone in from without. Even before one can blink an eye, there is an iron wall, an iron wall.
Holding up the written notice: To seize tigers and rhinoceroses, to distinguish dragons from snakes—this single phrase is utterly free from all entanglement. Why is this so?
Taibai never ascended the imperial hall; yet last night, flowers blossomed spontaneously upon his brush.

He pointed to the Dharma seat, which was steep and imposing on one side and intricately carved on all eight facets. "The King of Mount Sumeru and the Lamp—those with eyes see it; those who do not see it must ascend the seat.
Having said this, he ascended and spoke: "Follow the turning of my heels.

After offering incense and making prayers for the Emperor, he adjusted his robes and took his seat. He addressed the assembly, saying: "Great wisdom is profoundly clear, manifesting in a thousand transformations and ten thousand changes; great capacity is universally pervasive..."
It should be so. Seven long and eight wide. Yesterday, departing from Mount Rui, the staff-tip established the guest within the guests;
today, arriving at Mount Man, the shout below distinguishes the host within the hosts. Sweeping away the dens of wild foxes, he unleashes the claws and fangs of the lion.

Upon the "Awakened Stone," he arrays the perilous and divides the dangerous; by the "Drip-by-Drip Spring," he elevates the pure and stirs up the turbid. Until the howls of the monkeys resound through the ancient woods.
A tree. A tiger roars from a secluded crag; Yi-seong-ryeong leaps up to heaven; Daejak-dang bellows as it enters the sea. At such a time as this, tell me:
by whose power and grace does one receive this? He plants his staff upright and says: "Ten thousand years, a thousand ages—a single black cane."
Again, [the Master] raised an example concerning the founding patriarch, Chan Master Kongzhao. Every time he would call out, “Master! and [the student] would respond, “Yes.

Then [Kongzhao] would say, “Stay alert! and [the student] would again respond, “Yes. Finally, [Kongzhao] would say, “In the future, do not let others deceive you! and [the student] would respond, “Yes, yes. The Master commented:
“Old man Kongzhao performed a one-legged farce. Though the audience was large, those who laughed were few. Today, when I, Xiu Ruian, arrived here, I have not yet...”
Without even raising a hand, he gave the *zhuzhangzi* one more "spring" blow.
Then, calling out to the *zhuzhangzi* once, he struck the table with his staff and said, "Be alert! He struck the table again and said, "In the future, do not let others deceive you."
[The Master] strikes the desk twice and says: "Is there anyone who can understand and laugh at this? Thirty years hence, I shall give a small discourse (xiaocan):
'In the Jeta Grove, a thousand trees flourish; in the Pure Land, nine lotuses bloom. How many seekers of the profound mystery remain lost on the middle path?
[He] raises his whisk and says: 'Look! Look! Layman Lun, you usually only pick it up and play with it alone.'"
Enjoyment. Tonight, humans and devas are gathered together; ordinary and holy beings mingle. According to one's capacity, let us break through stinginess.

If you are one who establishes a family and builds a career—sitting not by day and sleeping not by night, striving with diligent persistence—he sweeps the whisk to his left side and strikes the meditation seat, saying:
"Realize it here! If you are one who ruins the family and scatters the career—hair uncombed and face unwashed—[he strikes].
To those who are utterly deluded and dazed, he waves his whisk toward the right side and strikes the meditation seat, saying: "Realize it here!

To the rest—those who seem to believe yet do not, those who wish to enter but have not yet entered, those who are half-cocked and half-hitched, and those who are half-green and half-yellow—he draws a single stroke with the whisk across his face and says:
"All of you, fall into line at once! Listen to the regulations separately! Suddenly, someone comes forward and says, "Newly grown..."
Old man, you have only just arrived; you are already flustered and at a loss. What will you do in five days’ time? Aha-ha!
Acquaintances fill the world, but how many can truly know one’s heart? Again, it is said that Luryuan addressed the assembly, saying:
"The essential meaning of the West is not easy to proclaim. At that moment, a monk stepped forward, and Luryuan struck him, saying: "What is this?"
At that moment, [the monk] poked his head out and immediately returned to the abbot’s quarters. The Master commented:
"To deploy a lightning-fast mechanism and employ a thunderbolt hand—this is not without the lineage of Ruyuan. It was only fitting that he should bump into a lacquer bucket.

If one’s eyes were like shooting stars, one would not have been able to return to the abbot’s quarters so easily. He suddenly took up his staff and said: "Is there no such person as this under the gate of Ruiyan?"
"Hūṃ hūṃ! Entering the hall:
Beneath the three rafters and before the seven-foot mat, there is a single phrase. All the monks under heaven, though they exhaust every skillful means, cannot fathom it;
they wish to raise it up, yet they cannot do so fully. Out of my grandmotherly concern, I shall briefly provide [it] for you."
"O people! This single thread of the Way allows no room for intellectual understanding; it requires only mind-to-mind transmission. After a long silence, he asked, "Do you understand?
It is like a ferry at the Baisi (Cai Shi) crossing."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following case: A monk asked Duofu, "What is the bamboo grove of Duofu?
Duofu said, "One stem, two stems, leaning. The monk said, "I do not understand. Duofu said, "Three stems, four stems, curved. The Master commented:
"A modest livelihood, a few meager provisions; handled with ease, its giving and withholding are worth observing. One must indeed..."
Only those with great merit may first attain it. Do you people wish to see a grove of bamboo? [The Master] strikes the staff and says:
"The moon sifts a ground of shadows; the wind shakes a sky of sound."

Ascending the hall for the Buddha-bath ceremony, the Master raised [the following] case: When the World-Honored One was first born, he pointed one finger toward heaven and one finger toward earth, walked seven steps, and looked around in the four directions, saying, "In the heavens above and on the earth below, I alone am the Honored One.

Yunmen said, "Had I seen him at that time, I would have struck him with a single blow of my staff and fed him to a dog, just to ensure peace throughout the world. The Master [continued]: [The Master then delivered his discourse.]

The Master picks up the case and says: "When the Old Barbarian came forth and offered this interpretation, he claimed that before him there was no one who had gone, and after him there would be no one to come.
Little did he know that a thousand years later, there would be a lame monk who refused to let it pass. Even so..."
The jade of Bian He: had it not been for Qin of the Han, how could the world have known of its value as the "Linked Cities" treasure?
Regarding the summer retreat’s small *can*: how can one take the Great Perfect Enlightenment (*mahā-vibuddha*) and make it one's own monastery? Wrong. It is the dwelling of body and mind in peace.
Falling into the ghost-cave of the Black Mountains; the Wisdom of Equality steams sand to make rice balls.
From antiquity until now, all the monks of the world have been ensnared, with no way to turn back. Tonight at Ruiyan, I have cut them off completely for you all.
It is fine to be carefree and unburdened, floating and drifting as one walks by mountains and waters. [He] brandishes his staff.

He brandishes a scorched staff, wears the sandals of Muzhou, and sits upon grass and stones. He drinks from the spring of Xuefeng and waves the fan of Yanguan, manifesting the function of the useless.
He bows to the tabby cat and salutes the white ox, proclaiming the command of the wordless. He rebukes Maitreya and reviles Śākyamuni;
though he thus possesses freedom in both killing and giving life, he strikes a circle with his whisk and says: "You must further penetrate this."
One cannot penetrate it. When intending to sit, one cannot sit; when intending to walk, one cannot walk. Do not blame me for being difficult to dwell with;
for the most part, the distinction between the monastic and the lay must be clear. Again, he cites an ancient saying:

"Within the realm of heaven and earth, amidst the universe, there is a single treasure, hidden within the mountain of form. Yunmen said: "Take the lantern and place it inside the Buddha hall. Bring [it] forth.
The lantern was brought from the mountain gate. The Master composed a verse, saying: "From the hidden smoke-filled village, the barking of dogs is heard;
Seeking to find it, yet no human dwelling appears. Suddenly, at the place where the bridge ends and the stream turns back, Three or four blossoms of emerald peach drift out."
Ascending the hall at the commencement of the summer retreat: Within the sacred regulations there is a secret key—three stars above and the crescent moon below.

Those who receive this must discern it clearly. During these ninety days, you must penetrate the teachings through practice. If you do not penetrate them, what you drink will be molten bronze and what you swallow will be glowing iron.
Upon returning from Mount Kai, he ascended the hall to deliver a discourse on the transmission of the Dharma, presenting three sheets of white paper.

"A thousand miles away, the same breeze blows"—this was the leftover spittle of the ancients; how can it compare to Ruiyan, who exchanged the extreme warmth of late spring for the gradual heat of early summer?
Nevertheless, the old monk atop the mountain has missed the mark, yet he does not even realize it.

Ascending the hall, he thanked the two halls for holding the whisk. "The eyes of humanity and the heavens; the governing principles of Buddhas and patriarchs. To hold fast or to let go—each and every instance depends on me.
If it depends on me, then it is so. Suddenly, the lanterns and pillars pierce through the nostrils of the whisk."
A white ox and a black cat have swapped the eyes of the whisk; how, then, shall one manage this?
Having long been accustomed to the battlefields, one fears not the rising clouds of war.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Before the fifteenth day, the pestle-tip blooms; after the fifteenth day, the scale-head bears fruit.
On the very fifteenth day, two *dhūtas* in the vegetable garden carry hoes and trim the weeds.
Suddenly, they drop them to the ground—yet they are but lumps of iron. You lot, you lacquer buckets, are dozing off on your long benches. Do you know?"
"What eggplants and gourds! Ha! [The Master] drank a mouthful and descended from the seat.

[On another occasion,] he ascended the hall to express his gratitude to the *jianshou* (storekeeper). He cited Master Dongshan Yan’s expression of gratitude to the *jianshou*, which he addressed to the assembly, saying:
"As for the matter of human life and destiny, first one must have the circle (○). To wish to achieve this circle, one must first guard against the circle. If one is truly..."

"○ Person. ○○. The Master held up the whisk and said: "The old man of Dongshan expressed his thanks for the supervision and collection of the harvest in such a way that he may be said to have fully exhausted the etiquette of a host.
Today, this mountain monk also expresses thanks for the supervision and collection; I cannot help but once again display our family tradition to look after you.
Regarding the life and nature of a person, the first thing required is... To wish to achieve this, one must first guard against..."
If one is a true person... do you understand? Dongshan’s circle, Ruiyan’s dot: neither adding to what is much, nor subtracting from what is little.
The Tathāgatas of the three periods of time share this same eye.

Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following case: Zhaozhou visited the Senior Hermitage Mistress and asked, "Is there anything? Is there anything? The Hermitage Mistress held up her fist. Zhaozhou said, "The water is too shallow; it is no place to moor a boat. He then visited the Junior Hermitage Mistress and asked, "Is there anything? Is there anything? She also held up her fist. Zhaozhou said, "It can kill and it can give life; it can let go and it can seize. He then prostrated himself. The Master offered this verse: The Senior and the Junior, both holding up their fists— One is shallow, the other is deep. To kill or to give life, to let go or to seize— Who can discern the source of these two masters? If you can see through them, you will know that the ancient path is not far off. But if you hesitate, you will surely fall into the weeds. Zhaozhou’s single word was like a thunderbolt; He struck the two women at once. If you can understand this, you will see that the Buddhas and Patriarchs are all here. If you cannot, you must look again. Do not mistake the fist for the truth; The fist is merely a finger pointing at the moon. If you grasp the fist, you lose the moon; If you seek the moon, you lose the fist. Only when you have cast both aside can you enter the gate. If you can do so, you will be a true successor of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. If you cannot, you are still wandering in the dark. Go ahead and try to test this; I shall wait for your answer. If you can speak, I shall grant you the seal of certification. If you cannot, you must repent. Do not say that the ancients were not thorough; They were simply testing you. If you can pass this test, you will be a person of great capacity. If you cannot, you are but a commoner. Do not doubt this; It is a matter of life and death. If you can understand this, you will realize that the Way is not something to be sought externally. It is right within your own hands. Do not look elsewhere; Look within yourself. If you can find it, you will be free from all delusion. If you cannot, you will remain bound by the cycle of birth and death. Therefore, I urge you: do not be negligent. Exert yourselves with all your might. This is the urgent call of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. Do not waste this precious human life. If you can act now, you will attain liberation. If you hesitate, you will suffer in vain. This is the essential teaching of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. Do not take it lightly. Reflect upon it deeply. If you can practice accordingly, you will surely attain the fruit of enlightenment. If you cannot, you will remain lost in the mundane world. Therefore, I exhort you: do not be idle. It is said: "The northern and southern islets are entirely lotus; one knows not where they bloom with partiality.
The traveler shifts his boat toward the north, surely because the scenic splendor lies on that side."

Small-scale *chanshi* (private instruction) upon the conclusion of the summer retreat: Listening to the rain, listening to the wind; eating gruel, eating rice—two five-hundred coins are originally but one thousand. Cuiyan said:
"Throughout this entire summer, I have been talking here and there with you brothers; look, are my eyebrows still there or not?
This is much like a young daughter-in-law using clever words to flatter her mother-in-law. Changqing said: "Born! Followed by a scavenging ruffian."
Baofu said, "The heart of a thief is always apprehensive; who would believe you? Yunmen said, "A barrier. This too is like a village woman imitating the beauty of another.
When Ruiyan proclaims in this manner, does he perhaps surpass the ancients by a head? After a long silence, he said: "It is easy to draw a sword and cleave through self and other;
it is difficult to push a mountain over and block off right and wrong. He then cited a monk’s question.
Regarding the Venerable Master Yunfeng Yue: "In the Western Heavens, they use a wax man as a test; here in this land, what do you use as a test?
Yunfeng replied, "An iron ball. The Master commented: "I have long heard that Yunfeng attained enlightenment when a wooden barrel hoop exploded.
It turns out his understanding was merely like this. Nevertheless, the heavens are high—who listens? The earth is vast—few are those who understand."

On the occasion of the Mid-Autumn Festival, he ascended the hall. While Changsha and Yangshan were admiring the moon, Yangshan said, "Everyone possesses this very thing, yet they simply cannot make use of it. Changsha said, "I have just now borrowed it for you to use.
Yangshan asked, "How do you use it? Changsha then gave him a kick, knocking him over. Yangshan said, "Right now you are like a great tiger!"
The Master picked up the case and said: "Daguan was right, but why such haste? Changsha’s approach is excellent, yet it is a pity.
Whether it can be used or not now, let us set it aside for a moment. He then made a gesture with his whisk as if pointing at the moon and asked:
"Do you all see this? Fortunately there is no place of partial illumination; yet there is still a time when it is not clear."
Ascending the hall: In the eighth and ninth months, with the white dew and cold dew seasons, the waters recede from the precipitous cliffs and mist enshrouds the ancient trees.
Yet the patch-robed monks refuse to let go; they merely bind their straw sandals and drag their staffs about, wandering eastward and seeking in the west.
Even if you were to employ every stratagem for nine years, thirty days, and thirty nights, you would still not depart from your current location. Suddenly—
He called out, "Venerable Elder! Stop, stop! Entering the Hall.
He then cited Xuefeng’s address to the assembly: "We have already met at Mount Wushi; we have already met at Wangzhou Pavilion;
we have already met before the Sangha Hall. When Guo Hu saw Baofu before the Sangha Hall, he asked him:
It is said: "If you meet at Wanzhou Pavilion on Mount Wushi, there is no need to ask. But what about meeting before the Sangha Hall? Baofu lowered his head and returned to the Sangha Hall;
Ehu shook out his sleeves and returned to the Abbot’s quarters. The Master commented:

"Black and white pieces divided like stars—a single game of chess. Master Zeng’s every move reveals the celestial mechanism. Within this lies the subtle art of seizing the corner and breaking through the pass."
Only Gehu and Baofu know this. Small Assembly for the Winter Solstice:
When the six yin lines are completely stripped away, the bald-headed broom stands in formation behind the gate; when the single yang line returns, life begins anew.
Wearing ear-cut straw sandals, dancing by the roadside, reaching every corner of the land—bells ring from the watchtowers and drums beat in the halls.
This draws forth a troop of old, gnarled logs who chatter away with their mouths agape; yet when have they ever known this news?
It is not that Ruiyan is showing off his chest or diminishing others' reputation; he simply wishes for the assembly here before him to turn their heads back.
Turning the head; turning the head and looking back. To discern the source where there is no source is to cause turmoil in the monastic groves that shall not cease.
Again, it is said: Mingzhao addressed the assembly, saying, "The wind here is somewhat harsh; let us return to a warm place to deliberate."

Mingzhao returned to the abbot’s quarters, and the assembly followed him inside. Mingzhao said, "As soon as you reach a warm place, you see people nodding off," and with his staff, he struck them all out at once.
The Master composed a verse: "The calculations made beforehand have already failed;
The arrangements made afterward are likewise not right. If there had been people of the present day in ancient times, They would not have fallen into the sleeves of others."

Ascending the hall on the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month: Two thousand years ago, a wild fox spirit, for no reason at all, breached the city walls at midnight and fled toward the Snowy Mountains.
One knows not how many stages he traversed before, upon seeing a star in the heavens, his two eyes were blinded.
"Bringing it upon future generations, their descendants will have to walk groping along the walls. Thus spoke Ruiyan; he too was merely increasing delusion through idle matters.

On New Year’s Eve, during the small *chan* assembly: "The year is spent and the age is exhausted; the night is still and the depth profound. With what shall we share [the Dharma] with the great assembly?"
This year, we shall roast the ox of Beichan, pour the wine of Caoshan, break apart the cake of Yunmen, and serve the tea of Zhaozhou.
These are matters of everyday routine for you all; nevertheless, I cannot help but bring forth this "dead cat's head" that has lain dormant for many years.
I shall strip its bones, scrape its marrow, mince it into fine pieces, and offer it as a humble hospitality. Striking the staff, he said: "As expected, how many of you are truly without thought?"
[The Master] calculated it. Having finished speaking, cold sweat flowed over his entire body. He raised the case again:
Guishan asked Yangshan, "I do not ask about the matter of the present; how is it regarding the matter of antiquity? Yangshan crossed his hands, stepped forward, and stood there.
Guishan said, "That is still the matter of the present. How is it regarding the matter of antiquity? Yangshan crossed his hands, stepped back, and stood there. Guishan said, "You..."
"You yield to me; I yield to you. The Master picked up the case and said: "From antiquity until now, advancing and retreating—the private matters of father and son have all been shaken out at once.
That they were shaken out is not in doubt, but as for saying 'you yield to me' and 'I yield to you,' how would you distinguish them? Three dice thrown, nineteen."
Ascending the hall on the first day of the year: the year is new, the moon is new, the days are new, and the times are new. Zen practice is new, the Buddha-dharma is new;
even the whisk and the staff are all brand new. How do you see this? (He strikes the floor with the staff. "The beginning of the year brings forth a new reign; all things are renewed."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Gautama is a dried-up dung-club; Bodhidharma is a discarded straw sandal. Monks cannot see through them;
they remain hidden deep within the breast. Enough, enough! At Ruiyan, I cleared them away all at once. In a place where there is nothing to grasp, I point out this manifest way of life.
He threw down his staff and asked: "How does this compare to Yunmen’s 'a single piece of firewood'?"
Ascending the hall, he said: "The Master sometimes is obscure; the Master sometimes is clear. When he is obscure, everyone rejoices;
when he is clear, everyone is vexed. Now, I shall cast this clarity that causes vexation aside to the left, and fling that obscurity that brings joy to the right.
Where, then, can one see the Master? Listen! [He spreads his hands and says: Finished."

Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the case of National Teacher Zhong. One day, the National Teacher called to his attendant. The attendant responded. This was repeated three times; the attendant responded three times.
The National Teacher said, "I thought it was I who was failing you, but it turns out it was you who were failing me.
The Master commented: "The National Teacher’s three calls—smoke gathers in layers of fresh green. The attendant’s three responses—the wind stirs fallen red petals."
"Piece by piece. Let this matter rest for now. I thought it was I who had failed you; it turns out it is you who have failed me.
How else shall we discuss this? After a long silence, he said: "This spring will pass once more; when will it be the year of our return?"

He sets it down and says: "Aha-ha! How extraordinary! This shallow thing is also profoundly deep. He draws a stroke with the whisk and says:
"Followers of the Chan school, simply investigate in this manner within these one hundred and twenty days. In this way, investigate. In this way, investigate.

"Study. Entering thus, realizing thus—yet, ultimately, what is it that is realized? [The Master] strikes the whisk and says: "Han Gan’s horse neighs across the fragrant grass; Dai Song’s ox lies down in the shade of the green willows. The World-Honored One called out, "Five-attainment immortal! [The immortal] replied, "Yes? The World-Honored One said, "Where have you been? The immortal was speechless. He called out to the Immortal, and the Immortal responded. The World-Honored One said, "Which one is the single penetration?
You ask me. The Master composed a verse: "Which one is the single penetration? You ask me. The profound gate has its hairless lock turned upside down; With a casual tug, it can be opened."
"Three old women sit facing each other. Tsk! He ascended the hall and said:

"In the mountains of Jing there is jade; he who obtains it does not find it within the mountains of Jing. In the waters of Chi there is a pearl; he who picks it up does not find it within the waters of Chi.
A patch-robed monk has the 'True Person of No Rank'; he who realizes it does not enter or exit through the face-gate."
Suddenly picking up his staff, he placed it across the desk and said, "Do you understand? A stone man crouches at the mouth of the river in Youzhou. He ascended the hall and raised an example:

A monk asked Zhimen, "What is it like when the lotus flower has not yet emerged from the water? [Zhimen replied,] "The lotus flower. [The monk asked,] "What is it like after the lotus flower has emerged from the water?
[Zhimen replied,] "The lotus leaf. The Master commented, "Great indeed is Zhimen; he only knows how to cut off the flow of all streams, but he cannot..."
"Following the waves and drifting with the current. Suddenly, someone asked Ruigan: "What is it like when the lotus has not yet emerged from the water?

"The lotus leaf. "What is it like after it has emerged from the water? "The lotus flower. Now tell me: is this cutting off the flow of all streams, or is it following the waves and drifting with the current? Investigate!
Ascending the hall to pray for clear weather, [the Master] struck with his staff and said: "With this stroke, I cut through ten thousand miles of deluded clouds.
He then drew a circle and said: "Releasing a single orb of the bright sun, the grasses and trees of the great earth receive this radiance;
every leaf and branch becomes lush and verdant. "Tell me, whose power and grace is this? He threw down the staff and said: "Zhuya of Mount Tiantai. (9)
The Master selected this passage. He ascended the hall and said: "A monk asked Zhaozhou, 'Does even a dog have Buddha-nature? Zhaozhou replied, 'No.
The monk said, 'All sentient beings, down to the most minute insects, possess Buddha-nature; why then does the dog not? Zhaozhou said, 'Because it has karmic consciousness.'"
The Master’s verse says: "When the wedge is removed, the wedge is taken out; Old Zhaozhou is truly unique. Unique, unique!
Three catties of iron behind the diamond-hard skull."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Water pours down before the crags; crickets chirp beneath the steps. When questioned by a monk, he has a mouth like a mute.

For one hundred and twenty days, he has played with the real as if it were the false. Holding up his whisk, he said: "Today, it suddenly emerges from the tip of this whisk—pure, naked, and starkly clear.
There is nothing to grasp. Do you see? He then threw it behind him and said: "And now it has entered into the nostrils!"
Ascending the hall, he said: "Autumn clouds and autumn waters, both lingering close. To tear open one's belly and gouge out one's heart—wild geese cry out as they pass through the emerald heights.
Thinking they have been forgotten, they mostly head toward the banks of fragrant grass on Lake Dongting. Who? The heavens of Chu are vast and wide, yet they do not know how to return.
This is a failure even before examination. The old man Wuzu’s little bit of livelihood has been entirely squandered by Ruiyan. Do not...
"Is there anyone who does not find this unsatisfying? He looks left and right and says, "This is the bottom line of Deshan.
On the Mid-Autumn Day, he ascends the hall and says: "The light of the moon is pure and bright; fundamentally it is neither full nor deficient. How laughable is Ma Boji!"
At this time, the sons were in a state of commotion, vying with one another to display their ineptitude. Some spoke of spiritual practice; some spoke of making offerings;

others brushed aside their sleeves and departed. Aha ha! To manifest the radiant glory of the original ground in such a manner—how does it differ from joining bamboo poles to reach the moon, or brandishing a staff to strike at the moon?
Ascending the hall, the Old Man of Ruiyan repays his debt: he was born with both ears deaf. When struck, he knows not where the Way lies; when questioned on Chan, he understands nothing of Chan.
Fearing the cold, he pulls up his cap and skirt; loving the cool, he loosens his waistband. Upper and lower garments rely upon one another without resentment;
from the beginning, both have had spacious stomachs.
Ascending the hall on the Double Ninth: This is the festival of the Double Ninth, the time when Yuanming gathered chrysanthemums. Yellow flowers are found everywhere;
how could they be limited to the eastern fence? If you do not believe me, just watch as I pluck a branch. (He raises his staff.)
Do you see? Though it is fine in the rain, it is even more extraordinary after the frost.
He ascended the hall and said, citing the story of King Zhao meeting Zhaozhou: Zhaozhou sat upright upon his meditation seat and said, "Great King, do you understand?"
The King said, “I do not understand. The Governor said, “Since my youth I have maintained the fast; now that I am old, I lack the strength to descend from my meditation seat when seeing someone.
The Master offered this verse: Mount Hua rises abruptly, piercing the azure heavens; It cuts off the earth’s axis with its myriad peaks.
Fan Lang passes beneath the mountain on his donkey, Hearing only the birds’ cries amidst the bustling spring breeze.
Master Xie, the Librarian, ascended the hall. He cited an ancient case: Once there was a monk sitting in the sutra hall who was not reading the sutras.
The Librarian asked him, "Venerable sir, why do you not read the sutras? The monk replied, "I do not know how to read characters. The Librarian said, "Why do you not ask someone else?
The monk then placed his hands together in *añjali* and asked, "What characters are these? The Librarian was left speechless. The Master commented: "Though this monk’s sutras..."
"Not looking. [The Master] translated the twelve divisions of the teachings into verse. Although the title of the canon is not mentioned here, he has swept away the writings of twenty-four schools.
He has finished his commentary and he understands it thoroughly. "Do you all see the structural joints? He struck the meditation seat and descended from it.

Ascending the hall, he said: "The fish play in the stream, rising and sinking; the birds soar through the forest, flying up and down. Yet how can one bear to see the wheat being reaped in the eastern garden and the rice being planted in the western fields?
The young girl plucks leaves to feed the silkworms, while the young lord raises his whip and gallops his horse. In truth, there is no difference between these things."
"Among you people on these long benches, spreading out your bowls and opening your mats to eat porridge and rice—has anyone ever bitten into a grain of sand?
Has anyone? No one? No one?"
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the case of Magu seeing Linji. Magu spread his sitting cloth and asked, "Of the twelve faces of Avalokiteśvara, which one is the correct one?
Linji stepped down from his meditation seat; with one hand he took the sitting cloth and with the other he seized Magu, saying, "Where has the twelve-faced Avalokiteśvara gone?
As Magu turned his body to sit down, Linji raised his staff and struck him.
Magu took up his staff and, seizing [the monk], they returned together to the abbot’s quarters. The Master commented:
"The great assembly, at this time of spring tasks, each carries their own burden of dust and soil, scattering it upon their own fields;
I do not blame them for that, but the mess is truly excessive."
A Small Sermon for the Summer Retreat. Before the fifteenth day of the fourth month, there is no decrease; after the fifteenth day of the seventh month, there is no increase.
Since there is neither increase nor decrease, let us set aside for a moment what comes before and after.
But as for the matter within these ninety days—how is it? He then held up his whisk and said: "If you can see it here, [you will find] the broken-legged cauldron."
I shall assist you from left and right. (He strikes the whisk. Here you hear it: the broken sand-pot. I shall pick it up and move it about with you from east to west.
If you see as if not seeing, or hear as if not hearing, you will inevitably have your eyes blinded and your ears blocked by the whisk of Ruiyan.
(He throws the whisk behind his back. Leap up to the Thirty-three Heavens!
[The Master] gives a shout. He then raises [the case]: Once while Yunyan was sweeping the ground, Daowu said, "You are being far too busy.
Yunyan said, "You must know that there is one who is not so busy. Daowu said, "If that is so, then there is a second moon.
Yunyan held up his broom and asked, "Which moon is this? Daowu stopped and left. The Master laughed heartily and said, "Great!"
Xiaoyunyan said, "I have not yet finished sweeping the ground. If one were a true descendant of Linji, how much time would it take to turn the broom handle upside down?
When Master Xiyuan of Nengren arrived, he ascended the hall and raised the following case: Master Rongfu visited Master Shixing. Master Da...
The Master ascended the hall. Taking up his staff, he pointed toward the left and said, "If it were not for my elder brother, Master Fuyong, it would have been very difficult to fully comprehend.
He then held up the staff and said, "Master Shixing’s arrangement was much like using mugwort broth in place of formal ritual.
Today at Ruiyan, although Elder Brother Nengren has arrived and we possess this staff, it simply does not..."
It is stirred! Why? Because both have emerged from the same teacher’s gate.

Entering the hall: Steep are the crags and rocks; luxuriant are the pines and creepers. Branches to the left and vines to the right, pulling crosswise and trailing vertically, they spread across the ground in a dense tangle.
How many are tripped up by them, yet instead blame the profusion of entanglements? Aha-ha! When you cannot leap out, what can you do?

"What can be done? He ascended the hall and raised the following case: A monk asked Yantou, "How is it when the ancient sail has not yet been hoisted? Yantou said, "The donkey in the back garden eats grass.
The monk asked again, "How is it after the ancient sail has been hoisted? Yantou said, "A small fish swallows a large fish. The Master composed a verse, saying:
In the back garden, the donkey eats grass; opening its mouth, its heart and liver are revealed. At the place where Pan Lang rode backward, who is able to discern it?
Another verse says: The small fish swallows the large fish; Its tail protrudes as a single stump. The old fisherman is drunk and unaware;
In vain he pulls at his fishing line.
The Small General Assembly for the End of the Summer Retreat: The master of the house rolls along, possessing both hands and feet, with neither front nor back.
Sometimes he hammers ice and fishes in deep mountains; sometimes he warms himself by the fire and fans himself in bustling markets.

It is truly laughable that these Chan practitioners dwell perpetually upon their meditation cushions, searching east and west, yet failing to have a single moment of direct realization. Now, at this time of *pravāraṇā* (the invitation to point out faults), [one must look within].
By what means shall this be verified? Tonight at Ruiyan, having no other choice, I cannot help but split open my own face and provide a skillful means.
He struck the meditation seat and said: "A gust of autumn wind grows cold as evening falls; it blows away three or four fragments of white cloud."
Again, he cites a case: A monk went to visit Zhaozhou. Zhaozhou called out, "Come closer! The monk approached. Zhaozhou said, "Go.
The Master [Zhaozhou] comments: "O assembly, this monk was already pitiable enough;
now, for no reason, he has been brought down by Zhaozhou’s single threadless cord."
Ascending the hall, he raised the following case: When the wind blew against the flagpole at Caoqi, the Sixth Patriarch saw two monks debating it.

One said, "The wind moves. The other said, "The banner moves. They argued back and forth without reaching a resolution. The Sixth Patriarch said, "It is not the wind that moves; it is not the banner that moves."
The benevolent one’s heart was moved; the two monks were struck with awe. The Master composed this verse: "Whispering yellow leaves bury the desolate path;
Misty floating clouds lock the wild hall. A single gust of west wind sweeps them all away; Only a few tall trees lean against the setting sun."
Ascending the hall: Turning the body, moving the feet, opening the mouth, revealing the teeth—clearly this is me; it is certainly not another.
Yet Zen monks refuse to find their enjoyment in the place of essential simplicity, preferring instead to toil wearily upon the road.
How truly a pity! How truly lamentable! I, Ruigan, out of my earnest and compassionate heart, cannot help but point out for you a place of rest. Please, take heed at once!
Quickly turn your heads! Return home early. [He] throws down his staff and says, "Ya ya!
The Small Sermon for the Eve of the Year: The year ends and the age concludes; the age concludes and the year ends.
There is a thing, pitch black, crooked and winding, jagged and rugged, just like an old plum tree of many years. It cannot be dragged and cannot be broken. Clouds...
The cage has no shadow; the wind shakes it, yet there is no sound. It stands vast and expansive upon ground where neither yin nor yang exists. Is there anyone who can realize this?
If you have not yet clarified the branches and joints, nor recognized the root and trunk, I, this mountain monk, cannot help but point it out for you all.
Suddenly he picks up his staff and raises it: "Aha! So, after all, it is just a staff. He then quotes a monk:
A monk asked Master Lingguan, “What is the Buddha? Lingguan stuck out his tongue to show him. The monk bowed.
Lingguan said, “What principle did you see that you immediately bowed? The monk said, “I thank the Master for showing me by sticking out his tongue.
Lingguan said, “Lately, an ulcer has grown on my tongue. The Master [Zhaozhou] commented: “To advance forward is to investigate; to retreat backward is to receive. This one—
The monk’s approach was thus abbreviated. Alas, he could not sit and cut off the tip of his own tongue of spiritual observation.

At that time, had he waited for the other to ask, "What principle have you seen? and then simply prostrated himself while letting out a great laugh, one can be certain that [the truth] would have been spat out, unable to be withheld.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Nanquan selling himself was merely greedy for small profit; Daowu dancing with his ritual tablet was nothing but a ghostly performance;
Baizhang rolling up the mat turned it into a failure; Zhaozhou offering tea was far too polite. As for Old Man Sui, he is even more without foundation.
When a monk asked about the true meaning of the Buddha-dharma, he instead replied, 'Has the wheat ripened in front of the mountain yet? Tsk! Tsk!"

A small-scale *sanchan* (general address) for the end of the summer retreat: There is the moment of the chick pecking and the hen pecking; the root of the illness is not shallow. There is no place to grasp; the traces of transgression are even deeper.
Have you not seen how the old master, throughout this entire summer, did not speak a single word with the monks?
He has already piled up a mountain of dust upon the ground of purity. A monk sighed to himself, saying: "I have merely passed my time in vain; I dare not hope for more."

When he was preaching the Buddha-dharma, [the student] managed to hear the two characters for "correct cause" (*zhengyin*). "He is too clever," the old master remarked. The elder casually said, "Dharma-uncle, do not speak so hastily.
If we discuss the 'correct cause,' there is not even a single character. [The student] was defeated before even being examined.
Having spoken thus, he then tapped his teeth and said, "Just now, without reason, it was improper to speak in such a way; it is very much like falling into a well and then clutching at the railing."
An old resident by the neighboring wall heard this and said, "What a fine pot of soup, yet it has been defiled by two mouse droppings!
If you scold me, I’ll let you have at my beak; if you spit at me, I’ll let you splash some water. Setting aside the ancients for a moment, consider this:
within those ninety days, there was not a single word that Ruiyan and his brothers did not discuss from east to west. Now tell me, which was that one phrase?
As a person, you should not hesitate to reveal a bit of news before the assembly; is there such a thing? Is there? After a long silence, he said:
"A true master! A true master! He then cited an old case: Formerly, a monk asked Baoning, "What is the Buddha?
Baoning replied, "An iron hammer with no hole. The Master commented: "Baoning of great stature could only say half of it. If someone were to ask me—"
Suiryak said to him, "A holeless iron hammer. Do you all understand? An iron hammer without a hole;
a holeless iron hammer—right before his face he hurls it, regardless of who it may be.
Ascending the hall: One summer has already passed; such is the nature of our lives. The eyebrows lie across the eyes; the nostrils rest upon the lips.
If you, all of you, have not yet resolved your doubts, simply search for your nostrils within the realm of the cold and still.
Be careful not to be careless; otherwise, you will lose everything at once, even your eyebrows.
Entering the hall, he said: "The clouds of Mount Yan, the moon of Mount Qiao—sometimes rolling up, sometimes spreading out; sometimes full, sometimes incomplete; two by two, three by three."

Wandering by morning and returning by evening, with the corner of one’s *kāṣāya* robe and the tip of one’s staff—carrying what should be carried and wrapping up what should be wrapped up—one may indeed find personal delight and joy.
But if you arrive at Ruiyan, you will certainly be beaten until the staff is broken. Why? Because what kind of time is this now?
