The old lady-in-law forces herself to act as if she were in her youth; she lavishly applies rouge and powder like a palace consort.
She pays no heed to the cold laughter of those around her, even as flowers are still being tucked into her hair.
Ascending the hall: It is just the first day of the first month, yet it is already the fifteenth day of the twelfth month.
Throughout the year, I have spoken to you all from this side and that, speaking crosswise and lengthwise; not a single word has proven efficacious.
Today, I cannot help but strip away my defenses and reveal my very heart and gallbladder to speak directly. [He descends from his seat.]

A Small Sermon on the Eve of the New Year: On the thirtieth day of the twelfth month, one year has come to its full end. Country folk call out to one another in competition, standing outside their gates holding torches.
Only the whisk of Ruiyan remains entirely unaware of the shifting of cold and heat or the passage of the seasons;
it stays perpetually bristling in the corner of the bed. To move it would be to become an adversary to gods and humans, and to the Buddhas and Patriarchs.

An enemy. Tonight, I shall take it up with my own hand. *He strikes the whisk.* "Striking horizontally and striking vertically, I only wish that this entire assembly will together understand it thoroughly.
If you remain as before, the ink on your hearts will remain pitch black. A-he-he! How can you blame me, this old monk? He then raised another case:
Bei Chan addressed the assembly on New Year’s Eve, saying: "The year is spent and the age is exhausted; there is no..."
"You may share the harvest with the villagers. For now, slaughter a white ox from the open pastures, cook millet rice, and by the glowing logs of fire, perform the village field music.
Pass the time in this manner. Why? To avoid leaning on others' doorways or huddling against others' walls, only to be called a 'lord' by the people of the age.
Having said this, he returned to the Abbot’s quarters. At that time, there was the Elder Yiyu, who entered the quarters...

Zhaozhou called out, "Master! A government official arrived at the gate. Zhaozhou asked, "What is it? The official said, "The authorities have summoned you, Master; you must not refuse to pay the fine.
Zhaozhou then pulled off his hat and threw it to the ground. The official picked it up.
Zhaozhou grabbed hold of him and cried, "Catch the thief! Catch the thief! The official, however, placed the hat over his own head and said, "It is cold; let me return this to you, Master."
Chan Hehe laughed loudly. The Master commented: "There was nothing unusual in his selection of ingredients, nor anything extraordinary in his arrangement;
yet, this was no small feat for Beichan. However, when scrutinized, it was still merely performing social etiquette with one's mouth.

Even though you, Senior Monk, understand how to join in the festive toasts at the table, you cannot avoid being measured by your own private assets. With a single stroke of his whisk, he said: "One document settles all accounts. Now tell me, what about Rui?
Yanguan, how would you establish [the teaching]? He tossed his whisk behind him and said, "Take care at nightfall.
He ascended the hall and said: "Chan need not be cultivated; the Way need not be studied. Let go, and let go further; peace and happiness, and peace and happiness again."

The old monks of the world do not recognize good from evil; they emerge in a chaotic clamor, hanging out a single pivot or displaying a single phrase, claiming, "I have revealed the meaning of this story.
Little do they realize that the moment the mind is conceived, it is already deviant; the moment the mouth opens, it is already wrong. After a long silence, he said:
"Wrong! Wrong!"
Master Xie gave a discourse at the hall upon receiving the scholar Guo Jiyi. He raised the case of Master Baiyun Wenzhun, who, when Guo Gongfu arrived, addressed the assembly, saying:
"Last night while on my pillow, I composed a mountain verse. It is not merely to thank Gongfu;
I intend for it to strip away the flesh-and-blood undergarments of all the monks in the world. He then said: "The Great Man Above, Qiu Yiji, Hua San..."
"One thousand, seventy, ten. Such a young man. Eight or nine sons. A fine gentleman. One may know the rites. The Master picked up [the staff] and said:
"Old Man Baiyun has a fine saying; alas, many have cast it aside into the armor of 'nothingness'."
Today, Ruiyan brings this forward to provide a commentary. Not only does he express his gratitude to the scholar Jiyi, but he intends to pierce the nostrils of all the monks in the world.
He then says: *Shang daren* (The Great Man of the Upper Realm). *Qiu yiji* (Qiu Yiji). *Hua sanqian* (Transformed three thousand).
*Qi shi shi* (Seventy scholars). *Er xiaosheng* (You, the young student). *Ba jiu zi* (Eight or nine children). *Jiazuo ren* (Excellent work, benevolence). *Keshi li* (One may know the rites).
[He] threw down his whisk and descended from the seat.

[Then he] ascended the hall and said: "I cite the case where an outsider asked the World-Honored One: 'I do not ask about having words; I do not ask about having no words. The World-Honored One remained silent for a long while."
The outsider said, "World-Honored One, with your great kindness and great compassion, you have cleared away the clouds of my delusion and enabled me to enter.
The Master composed this verse: Holding a brick in hand, he hurls it into the air; It surely strikes his own head.
The resulting pain is difficult to describe; He rubs the spot himself and then goes home.
Ascending the hall, Master Zihu addressed the assembly, saying: "For over thirty years I have resided at Zihu; my strength for the morning and evening gruel and rice is coarse enough.
Every day I make three or two rounds upon the mountain. I ask you all: do you understand? The Master commented:
"You old fellow! Though you lack even a single point of Buddha-dharma in your body or mind, you still wish to hammer out a needle to make it into a hook.
If I were this mountain monk, I would not do so. For three or four years I have dwelt at Ruiyan, carrying the burden of right and wrong upon my own shoulders alone."
A snake swallowing a turtle’s nose; a dog biting a dog. Each and every thing is perfectly clear—there is no need for deliberation.

This is the small *canyuan* (general address) for the summer retreat. Cold and heat shift; time passes in an instant. In the blink of an eye, we find ourselves once again at the commencement of the summer retreat.
Although this mountain monk and the assembly present here have our eyebrows joined and our nostrils aligned, nevertheless, each must eat his own rice.
"Eating, each eats his own filth; defecating, each defecates his own; sleeping, each sleeps on his own bed; dreaming, each dreams his own. This is indeed so.
Suddenly, when it becomes improper, with a light pinch, one’s head turns red and face flushes. After a long while, he said: 'Xuefeng spoke to Yantou.
He then raised the story of the woman emerging from samādhi, and the Master composed a verse: 'Bao Shu places eyebrows beneath his eyes.'"
The elder leaned his ear toward the master’s mouth. Suddenly, meeting on a narrow path, what kind of faces do these two have?
I request the Abbot to ascend the hall. Exert yourself with diligence; set a strict limit. Whether right or wrong, cut it away! Suddenly, a topknot protrudes from the forehead;
round and full, like a broken oil lamp in a corner of the wall within an ancient hall.
The late Master Fojian’s final letter has arrived. As I offer incense before his altar, I reflect: that old monk had originally no fixed direction;
he was simply a head of hemp, yet he produced all manner of complications. For no reason, I too have been caught up in his entanglements;
my pillar of shame has toppled over. Bearing both resentment and gratitude, holding both sorrow and laughter, I burn this single stick of incense as an offering.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The ancients said, 'Ten days have passed since the summer retreat began; what of Hanshan?
Others said, 'Ten days have passed since the summer retreat began; what of the water buffalo? Here at Ruiyan, it is not so."
It has been ten days since the summer retreat began. A man from Cold Mountain leads a water buffalo toward the banks of Double-Brow Pond to graze.
Suddenly, he goes mad and rushes before the monks' hall, laughing at you lot of dozing fellows: "Riding one buffalo, you go looking for another buffalo!
You don't realize that whether there are a thousand or ten thousand heads, they are fundamentally just this one head. With a single grunt, he lets out a roar.
Descend from your seats.
[The Master] ascends the hall and says: A monk once set out for Mount Tai. On the road, he met an old woman and asked, "Which way does the path to Mount Tai go?
The woman said, "Go straight ahead. Just as the monk had taken two or three steps, the woman said, "What a fine master!"
He then departed in this manner. The monk reported this to Zhaozhou. Zhaozhou said, "Wait; I shall go and see through that old woman. Zhaozhou went there and asked her the same question;
the old woman answered him in the same way. Upon returning, Zhaozhou said to the assembly, "The old woman of Mount Tai has been seen through by me.
The Master composed a verse: "A fresh flower has newly blossomed red before the courtyard; its fragrance wafts..."
The fragrant scent intoxicates the bees; when the young lord sees it, his poetic inspiration is stirred. He blows his jade flute upside down, playing amidst the spring breeze.
Dharma-kinsmen, ascend to the hall: I have a single pivot, held up face-to-face. It is like striking metal and stone, like playing the *yunchi* pipes.
If one is not a true connoisseur, who can know it?
While traveling, he ascended the hall: "The tortoise-nosed snake of the South Mountain; the white-fanged tiger of the North Mountain.
At the third watch of the night, suddenly they spring to bite. The Great Being of Universal Penetration from India, seeing this injustice, let out a shout and brought them to a halt.
This mountain monk was just then dreaming by the side of the tangerine grove pavilion when he was startled awake by him. With a laugh, he returned. Now tell me: after returning, what then?"
"How so? The alert stone sprouts long bamboo shoots; drop by drop, the spring overturns vast waves.
This was the discourse given by Layman Liangshan upon ascending the hall. He recounted how Danxia visited Layman Pang and encountered his daughter, Lingzhao, on the road.
He asked, "Is the Layman at home? Lingzhao set down her vegetable basket and stood with her hands folded. Danxia asked again, "The Layman?"
"Is he here? The woman lifted her vegetable basket and walked away. Danxia then turned back. The woman recounted the previous conversation to the layman.
The layman asked, "Is Danxia here? The woman said, "He has gone. The layman said, "This too is like smearing red earth on a cow's udder.
The Master’s verse says: The younger sister takes colored silk to sew a flower-patterned robe; Half is deep blue, half is...
The red [flowers] were all stolen away by thieves at once; the wife beats her breast in vain.
Rainy and sour is the Cold Food Festival; the sun nurtures the Qingming. In groups of threes and twos, they call out to one another for the spring outing.

For those of the Chan school, there is no place to lodge their hidden sentiments; they lean their black staffs upside down against stone screens. They idly listen as the cuckoo at the crag calls out, note by note.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Awakening to the Way through sound. He struck the meditation seat and asked, "Is this not sound?
How do you awaken to the Way? "Illuminating the Mind through form. He held up his whisk and asked, "Is this not form? How do you illuminate the Mind?"

"Even if you were to realize it and understand it clearly, I would still question you: When the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara buys sesame cakes with money, why is it that as soon as he lets go of his hand, they turn out to be steamed buns? He gave a shout and descended from the seat.

At the conclusion of the summer retreat, the Master ascended the hall. He raised the following case: A monk asked Yunmen, "At the beginning of autumn and the end of summer, if someone suddenly questions you on the road ahead, with what will you respond?
Yunmen said, "The assembly, step back! The monk asked, "Where does the fault lie? Yunmen said, "Bring me back the payment for my ninety days' worth of rice.
The Master commented: "To enter a tiger's den and seek out its cub is no easy task. How could this monk compete [with Yunmen]?"
"Nai dies on level ground. Does the great assembly wish to recognize Yunmen? One foot short, one foot long.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the example of Ciming, who kept a basin of water in his room. Across the top of the basin he laid a sword, and upon the sword he placed a pair of straw sandals.
Whenever a monk entered, he would point at them; if the monk hesitated, he would strike him. The Master composed a verse, which begins: "The hundred flowers..."
The whip flashes through the thickets as he gallops past; how much brilliance and elegance there is! The unexamined scholar peeks at him with bated breath;
his heart is filled with an old sorrow he cannot dispel.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The autumn mountain colors grow old; autumn tree leaves fall; autumn clouds cast chaotic shadows; autumn waters are clear and still.
Stretching out the hand or drawing it back—when sought, it cannot be grasped. Opening the eyes or closing them—it has no form when looked upon.

The monks of the Five Lakes, with their disheveled robes and loose gowns, yawning and grinning, where could they possibly weigh this? How could they match it here? Yet even the old fellow of Ruiyan does not..."
How could one dare to compare their weight with him? Why? Because the measure is clear and distinct. Ascending the hall, he raised the case:
Once, when Danxia arrived at a village monastery, it was cold. He took a wooden Buddha and burned it in the brazier.
When the monastery master saw this, he said, "How can you burn my wooden Buddha? Danxia poked at the ashes with his staff and said, "I am burning for the sake of the *śarīra* (relics)."
The host said, "How could a wooden Buddha have *śarīra*? Xiang said, "Since there are no *śarīra*, why do you blame me?

Later, the host's eyebrows and beard fell out. The Master composed a verse: "The village elder, for a certain matter, consulted a sorcerer; The sorcerer revealed his innermost thoughts regarding fortune and misfortune.
He obtained gold and his family became wealthy and noble, Yet for many years he vainly gave rise to doubts."
Ascending the hall on the Winter Solstice, a monk asked: "I recall a monk asking Zhaozhou, 'Does a dog have Buddha-nature?
Zhaozhou replied, 'No. What is the meaning of this? The Master replied: "It is the sword that kills, the sword that gives life. The monk pressed further:
"All sentient beings, down to the smallest insect, possess Buddha-nature. Why then does the dog have none? The Master replied: "One who comes to sell jewels has run into a blind Persian."

The questioner said: "Zhaozhou said, 'It is because he still possesses the consciousness of karmic activity. What does this mean? The answer was: "When the ocean dries up, its bottom will finally be seen;
when a person dies, their mind is no longer known. The questioner continued: "A monk asked again, 'Does a dog have Buddha-nature or not? Zhaozhou replied, 'Yes.'"
The Master replied, “A living-man sword; a man-killing blade. The student pressed, “Since it exists, why does it enter this skin bag?
The Master replied, “A hunting dog chases after clods of earth; a lion bites a man. The student pressed, “Zhaozhou said, ‘Knowing it yet deliberately committing it’—what does that mean?

The Master replied, “When one trusts in the directness within the direct, who would suspect benevolence or lack thereof? The student pressed, “The embroidered mandarin ducks are displayed for you to behold.”

"I do not pass on the golden needle to others. The Master then said: "In the past, Duke Xi of Lu ascended the observation tower and recorded the clouds and atmospheric phenomena to verify the auspiciousness of the moment.
Although Ruiyan lacks such ability, I too must follow suit in this inversion.
[Holding his whisk,] he pointed east and said, 'On this side are yellow clouds. He then pointed west and said, 'On that side are white clouds. Now, as for the record—"
For what purpose did he compose these characters? He said: "The attendant must not leak any news.
When the Venerable Nengren arrives, he shall ascend the hall. To the east, south, west, and north of the sea, there lies within it the Great Dragon Pond of Yandang."

Layer upon layer stand ten-thousand-fathom precipices; falling drop by drop cascade thousand-fathom waterfalls. An old man with white hair sits on the ground for many years, doing nothing but watching.

Hearing the sound of a drum strike once from the watchtower atop the mountain, he turns his head and begins to deliberate upon the subtle and great Dharma-gate with the "Sleeping Man on the Awakened Stone. There is no lack of deliberation; but lift it up!
Kāśyapa Huán said, "Now tell me, what is this? Ló Gōng (Luopu) Shines in a Mirror. Ascending the hall, he said:
"In studying the Way and practicing Chan, there is no other expedient. That which is within the clamor must be clear within stillness; that which is within stillness must be realized amidst clamor.
Cut off both extremes and forge them into a single whole. When joy arises, raise a fist of wrath; when affliction appears, show a face of laughter."
A-he-he! When Ruiyan speaks in this manner, he is much like a crab falling into boiling water—every limb and claw exposed all at once. This is the small *chan* (sermon) for the summer retreat:
Heart-mind upon heart-mind, it is like a clumsy woman threading a needle; Wisdom upon wisdom, it is like a sorcerer scolding the local deity; Way upon way.
A dwarf carries a wicker basket on his shoulder. Buddha after Buddha. A crow pecks at rotten bones.
This night at Ruiyan, I have shaken out every single one of my three hundred and sixty joints and eighty-four thousand pores. Those whose eyes flicker and move—

Let it be as it is, scattered and fragmentary. Take it away; gather it up. Should one happen to be dazed and ignorant, there is no avoiding gathering it in for oneself, collecting it within, and concealing it inside.
Just wait for the ninety days ahead, when—amidst tea and rice—one will bite crosswise and swallow vertically;
while walking or sitting, one will look east and search west. Suddenly, with a stumble or a slip of the hand, one falls to the ground.
[The Master] struck [the monk]. The mountain monk, thereupon, was not afraid of shame; he stripped away his mask and, extending his hands, said:
"I entrust them both to you. He raised [his staff] and said: A monk asked Yunmen, "What is the place where all Buddhas emerge?
Yunmen said, "On the water above the Eastern Mountain. Later, Yuanwu said, "If it were Tianning, it would not be so. Suppose someone were to ask..."
"What is the place from which all Buddhas emerge? A fragrant breeze comes from the south; the halls and pavilions grow cool. The Master commented:
"One is a limping fellow, the other is a bald-headed fellow; they illuminate each other, so they are true masters.
Yet, pine and cypress remain green for a thousand years, but they do not suit the tastes of the people of this age."
The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Duanyue of Guoqing Jiaozhong Chan Monastery on Mount Tiantai, Compiled by the Attendant.
The entire great earth is this gate of liberation. Why is it that when one reaches out with one’s hand to pull oneself through, one cannot enter? *He gives a shout.*
"Hai! You do not know how to be a guest; you have troubled the host.
In the Buddha Hall, those sitting stand, and those standing sit. I am you; you are me. Ultimately, who is it that burns incense and prostrates?
Inserting the incense, he says: "How could this possibly avoid falling into idle chatter?"

In the Hall of the Grand Preceptor, his grand strategies were deployed and his profound counsels unfolded in secrecy. The浩然 (hàoqì) spirit within his breast far surpassed that of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou.
Fragrance billows from the jade incense burner for nearly a thousand autumns.
The Abbot: "This one barrier of mine has no back and no front. If you intend to step forward, the net is already over your head.
Having ascended the seat and finished offering incense in honor of the Emperor, he said: "To the north of Tiantai and south of the Stone Bridge, there lies a monastery known as Fangguang."
Now, let this old monk—half-witted and half-demented, half-deaf and half-mute—act as the master.
With Hanshan and Shide holding fast at the pass, Fenggan shall then lead five hundred headless fellows.
Let us all join in effort to snap the staffs and cut through the straw sandals; each extending a hand to support the mountain-axe, until the three sides are reached.
The clouds cleared; the winds of the entire land became pure. Woodsmen and herdsmen called out in joy, while birds and fish leaped for delight.
At such a time as this, to whom does the merit belong? One burner of aloeswood incense offers thanks to Lü Qiū. Again, he cites Hánshān and Shídé asking Abbot Fēnggān:
"When an ancient mirror is not polished, how can it reflect? Fēnggān said: "The ice-pitcher contains no image. The monkey—
The monkey probes the moon in the water. Hanshan said, "This is not a light that illuminates. He further requested, "Please speak.
Fenggan said, "Since you cannot bring forth the ten thousand virtues, what am I supposed to say? The two men bowed and withdrew. The Master commented, "Fortunately, this is a fine ancient mirror;
for no reason, it has been forcibly defiled with paintings by Hanshan, Shidi, and Fenggan. How clear and bright it was!"
It is gone! The new state is pure and clear. Unable to restrain my impatience, I cannot help but elaborate further. Holding up his whisk, he said:
"Without waiting for it to be hoisted high, Chiyou has already lost his majesty."

That evening, there was a small assembly for instruction. To raise the banner of the Dharma and establish the fundamental purpose, he manifested a fully perfected forge that requires no contrived arrangement.

Extending to wondrous monks and receiving the elite stream, he employs the tongs and hammer of one's own original portion; what harm is there in such expedient deployment? With the total capacity firmly grasped, illumination and function proceed in tandem.
A single thread is released; host and guest stand facing one another. This is the ordinary protocol of Xingguoqing Temple.
Suddenly, as if two mountain streams flow—sometimes slow, sometimes surging—and five peaks give rise to clouds—sometimes low, sometimes high—how then can one settle upon the truth?
After a long silence, he said: "Boya plays the zither. He then raised another case concerning Chan Master Yongming Qian. Because a monk asked him:
"What did Bodhidharma transmit when he came from the West? Yongming said, "He transmitted a tally-stick. A monk asked, "If that is so, then there are dharmas outside the mind.
Yongming said, "There are no dharmas within the mind. The Master commented: "The questioner was like striking at empty space with a staff."
The answerer’s response was like using a knife to cut water; it was merely the talk of those who have studied the words superficially, buried alive within their own manuals.
I dare ask the great assembly: When Bodhidharma came from the West, what exactly did he transmit? [He] brandished his whisk and said: "The wind sweeps through the dragon’s beard;
the moon shakes the phoenix’s tail."
The following day, for the sake of the Grand Preceptor, Duke of Yue, he ascended the hall and said: "The Great Balance operates alone, shaking the very heavens and earth;
the Great Function is fully wielded, hurrying on the sun and moon. Directly beneath him, he bears the True Seal of Vairocana and presses down the precious sword from the royal armory.
One life and one death—his strategy and tactics are complete; one release and one withdrawal—his civil and martial arts are fully equipped. He subdues the dog-herb (the wild weeds)."
Against the northern barbarians, he rebuked the serpent-beasts; against the western Rong tribes, he left behind a virtue that endures for all living beings.

His great achievements are engraved upon the ritual tripods. Thus, he transcends past and present, walking alone amidst the clouds and mists. To him, appearing and disappearing within birth and death is like strolling through a garden.
At such a time as this, how is it? [He] strikes the whisk and says: "Without leaving the world of the azure command-tent, his entire body is already here."
In the Palace of the Brahma King, the session is concluded. The sound of the purple flute has ceased as the moon hangs low; smiling, he points to Mount Penglai and Yingzhou as his ancestral home.
Not finding the Twelve Jade Towers, he reaches out to grasp the immortal crane and walks through the mists and clouds.
At the Nirvana Hall, he ascended the seat and said: "From the Deer Park at the beginning until the Bahudhika River at the end—within these two intervals—I have never spoken a single word.
Great assembly! This Yellow-Faced Gautama is full of falsehoods and short on truth; he offers this humble confession, which no one can overturn.
Year after year, the flowers bloom in competition during the fragrant season. He struck the meditation seat and said: "A single gust of eastern wind leaves them all in disarray."
Ascending the hall on the first day of the third month: Pear blossoms and plum blossoms are white; apricot blossoms and peach blossoms are red. This is the true Eye of the True Dharma;
this is the ancient Heart-essence of the Buddhas. Old Lingyun—when has he ever seen it in a dream?
Those who claim to have spoken of it are all merely uttering empty falsehoods. How vexing is the old fisherman of Lujiang, who turns the fishing line backward to stir the spring breeze!
Ascending the hall, he said: "The golden Buddha does not pass through the furnace; the Daoist recites 'su-lo. The wooden Buddha does not pass through the fire;
at Mount Song, the hearth was struck and fell. The clay Buddha does not pass through the water; Zhong Kui scares away the little ghosts. The true Buddha sits within the house.
*Sha!* Old man Zhaozhou has been exposed! If you still do not understand, listen further as Guoqing tears open his own face."
Reveal it and look! [The Master] makes a gesture with his hands as if parting his face. "How is this like Master Baogong of Zhongshan?
This is the incense offering for the memorial of Chan Master Fojian. "You are a monk from Sichuan; I am a monk from Zhejiang.
When we meet and see one another, it is as if we have never met before. Why then do we become enemies today? Have you not heard it said: 'Stinking meat attracts flies'?"
Ascending the hall on the eighth day of the fourth month: The crimson sun rises, and the eye of wisdom is clear and unclouded;
the white clouds emerge, and the countenance of compassion is revealed and unobstructed. The forest trees interlace like the *svastika* upon his breast;
the peaks and ridges overlap as the thousand-petaled lotus beneath his feet. What a truly natural Śākyamuni! If you say he was only born today into the family of the Brahmā-king, it is a pity.
"Alas, the Buddha! Alas, the Buddha! This is the small *chan* (meditation) discourse for the summer retreat.
To expand upon the essential points of the Dharma: within a single shout, one distinguishes host and guest;

in the great unfolding of the school’s fundamental principles, the three phrases encompass both killing and giving life. These are the skills of our predecessors, acquired through stealth and cunning. As for this mountain monk...
Born with both ears deaf and both eyes blind, unable to push away or pull toward, he is huddled and muddled, utterly simple and unrefined.

During the one hundred and twenty days of summer retreat, although he walked, stayed, sat, and slept together with the great assembly, he lacked even the slightest display of needlework or threadwork. Nevertheless, outside the mountain gate were two golden [bells].
Gang! Why do you glare with bulging eyes and knit brows? Why do you clench your fists and brandish your mace? *Hūṃ, hūṃ!* Again, he raised the case:
Once, when the two head monks of the two halls were disputing over a cat, Nanquan picked it up and said, "If you can speak, I shall not kill it.
The two halls were speechless; Nanquan then killed the cat. That evening, when Zhaozhou returned, Nanquan recounted the previous conversation. Zhaozhou—
Taking his straw sandals and placing them upon his head, he went out. Nanquan said, "Had you been here, you would have saved the cat.
The Master composed a verse: "Sending off spring, I wish to raise my golden goblet; But with a guest whose chest remains closed, how can we discuss it?
Having drunk a cup myself and returned home, I joyfully encounter the household's merriment at twilight."
The Head Official (Shoushou) took up the whisk and ascended the hall. "The void vanishes; lift your head and you strike your own skull.

The great earth sinks flat; move your foot and you kick your own thumb. Every one of the assembly at Guoqing has blood beneath their skin and sinews within their eyes—have you ever been like this or not?
If you hesitate, you must look with eyes raised high. He cast down the whisk.
Behind him, he said: "A fragment of cloud returns like an army. He threw down his staff and said: "Flowing water departs as if flying.
Ascending the hall, he raised the case of Sansheng asking Xuefeng: "The scaled dragon that has passed through the net—what do you take for food? Feng replied: [He remained silent].
"I will wait for you to emerge from the net before I speak to you. The Master said, "A man of virtue with fifteen hundred followers, yet you do not even recognize the pivot of the teaching.
Feng said, "This old monk’s administrative duties are too numerous. The Master commented: "As a guest, one dances like a phoenix in the crimson sky;
as a host, one gallops like a dragon across the azure heavens. These two great elders may truly be called one guest and one host, each to the other."
This is appropriate. But alas, these "crows in the fence" and "frogs in the well" clamor and chirp about in confusion, not knowing where they are headed.
[The Master] ascends the hall: Within the shadows of Five Peaks, amidst the sounds of the Twin Streams, there is a great treasury, radiant on all eight sides.
Everyone here has spent so much time [here]; for what reason can you not see it with your eyes, nor grasp it through speech? This mountain monk—
Today, I open it up directly. Holding up his staff, he says: "This is Mipamopa’s single-pronged pitchfork.
Holding the staff crosswise, he says: "This is Daowu’s single-edged sword. Drawing three circular diagrams, he says:
"These are Xuefeng’s three wooden balls. A-he-he! Yet they do not resemble the wind atop the flagpole on the road to Caoxi."
The banner moves; when the banner moves, the wind comes from the south, the north, the west, and the east.
On the sixteenth day of the sixth month, at the commencement of the season of autumn, he ascended the hall. Deshan lowered his head; Jia Shan nodded his head;
Jueyi held up a finger; Xuansha broke off a toe. Raising his staff, he said: "All of this does not go beyond my mountain monk."
[The Master] raised his whisk. How can this be seen? He struck the whisk and said: "When a single leaf falls, autumn comes to the whole world.
When Master Zhishan Huangbo arrived, [the Master] ascended the hall to express thanks for the steward. He said: "The life-vein of the Buddhas and Patriarchs is as precarious as a hanging thread.

To support it with bare hands requires a true master. As for calculating with counting sticks and tally marks, and debating points of doctrine—the matter of victory and defeat has not yet been asked."
"Everyone, Huangbo struck Linji with sixty blows of his black staff. Now tell me, which one of them did not get hit?
After a long silence, he said: 'The clear-eyed cannot be deceived.'"
Small Session for the End of the Summer Retreat. For the long period of one hundred and twenty days, the minds of the assembly have been like walls;

they laugh as they gaze upon the True Person of No Rank, who freely enters and exits through the gateway of the face. This old mountain-dweller has won a messy victory, following along with the scavenging search.

For now, let us avoid the horizontal strikes and vertical blows; let us lift from the left and support from the right. Let us extract the speck of dust from the eye and pull out the nail from behind the head.

Let us untie the glue that leaves no residue and remove the bond that binds nothing. Now that this summer retreat has reached its completion, we are fortunate to have the aged iron sour cakes left over from Dongshan.
We shall break them apart and offer them as a universal供养 (pūjā). He strikes the staff and says: "It fills one to the brim and puts an end to hunger."
Cease your resentment; there will surely come a time when you receive a punch for throwing one yourself. Again, he raised an old case:
A monk asked Shuangquan, "In the Western Heavens, they take the wax man as proof; I wonder what is taken as proof here? Shuangquan said, "The feet do not touch the ground."
The Master said: "Do you all see the Two Springs? If someone were suddenly to ask about the Two Streams, you should simply answer him:
'Their heads do not touch the sky. Do you all recognize the Two Streams? Listen to this verse: 'Feet do not tread the ground; Heads do not touch the sky.
As soon as you recognize the Two Streams, You shall see the Two Springs. Questioning has its past and present; answering is free from the biased and the orthodox. If..."
Before dawn, he chewed gelsemium (huanglian) finely.

He ascended the hall and said: "On the mountain peak are horns of unusual shape and lustrous fur; at the bottom of the stream are fish with scales like brocade and vermilion tails. Each possesses its own single life-force."
"All are within this mountain monk’s hands. Today, I loosen the tether;
let them gallop at will, let them soar and cry out at will, let them swim and wander at will, let them hide and leap at will—who is there to govern you?
While all quarters are densely covered by a net that reaches to the heavens," [the Master] struck the meditation seat and descended.

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Sifting sand to find gold, cleaving rock to find jade, drawing a bow to catch birds, casting a line to catch fish—these are things sought and taken by all people;
there is nothing that cannot be obtained. Yet for us monks alone, when we seek to reach 'existence,' it leaves the great earth empty;
when we seek to reach 'non-existence,' it fills the vast void. Tell me, why is this so?"
Wiping away the written characters, descend from your seats.
On this winter solstice small *chán*: vast and nebulous, muddled and indistinct—what a wonderful Dharma-gate of Great Peace and Bliss!

Without cause, it underwent a single transformation, and suddenly there were heaven and earth, sun and moon; they revolve through the twenty-four energies and turn the seventy-two seasonal signs. For...
Expansion becomes contraction; prosperity becomes decline; death becomes birth; waning becomes waxing. From the Buddhas and Patriarchs above, these have been set aside and left unexamined.
Yet you people fall into their midst, your minds busily occupied, your mouths incessantly chattering, and your hands never ceasing their toil.
Their feet do not stay still; they are seven topsy-turvy and eight upside-down, or eight upside-down and seven topsy-turvy. When will there be rest?
Tonight at Guoqing, amidst this state that is neither yin nor yang, I shall point out for all the Dharma-gate of Great Peace and Bliss.
Let everyone enter it together, realize it together, and dwell together within this Dharma-gate of Great Peace and Bliss. (He strikes the whisk. Beneath the golden incense burner is the Iron Kunlun.
Again, he raised the case: One day, Master Fenyang held up his staff and said to the assembly, "If you recognize this staff, your journey as a wandering monk is finished.
The Master commented: "O Great Assembly! If one does not extinguish a spark, it will burn across the plains;
if one does not stop a mere drop, it will flood the heavens. For Fenyang to act toward people in such a manner—disaster is born!"
The Head Official (Xie) held the whisk and ascended the hall. It was the season when the clouds gather to mark the beginning of winter;
he commanded three Zen practitioners to each take up a brush and compete in writing this single character within the empty space.

Whether they drew a stroke or applied a dot, or whether their strokes and dots were incomplete—it was like Confucius and Duke Xi of Lu, where one could neither discern the text nor know its meaning. You all must...
"Do you understand? He then looked around to his left and right, spat once, and descended from the seat.
Upon ascending the hall for the discourse, he cited the case where Grand Master Lu Xuan asked Nanquan, "What is your surname? Nanquan replied, "My surname is Wang. Lu Xuan said:
"Are there also attendants? Quan said, "The four ministers are not obscure. Guoquan asked, "In what position does the King reside?
Quan said, "Moss grows upon the jade palace. Guoquan asked, "What is it like when moss grows upon the jade palace? Quan said, "He does not occupy the central throne."
The Master held up the staff and said: "Chasing what is in front, pursuing what is behind; chasing what is behind, following what is in front.
Even Grand Officer Lu Xian still does not know. If he did know—*suddenly seizing the staff—he said*: 'Master Wang! Master Wang!'"

You followers of Zen go to the east to inquire and to the west to study, yet when it comes to a single question, you utterly fail to find its head or nose.
I, this mountain monk, have a "Pill for All Ills"; though it possesses no great efficacy, when encountering those such as these...
People, it is exactly what is needed. Do you understand? After a long silence, he said: "Let it go.
On the fifteenth day of the ninth month, he ascended the hall and said: "Smoke stretches across the vast fields; wild geese form patterns in the long sky.
Jade dew drips upon eight or nine branches of yellow chrysanthemums; the golden wind shears away three or two fragments of crimson maple. Though the livelihood of my house is cold,"
"Dàn. He suddenly picked up his staff and said, "To take it, there is no prohibition. Zuo said, "To use it, there is no end.
Suddenly, if someone were to ask, "Venerable Sir, you have again used the property of the Sangha for your own private enjoyment," he would simply reply, "Not only today."
How many matters from the past are all contained within the unspoken.

Ascending the hall, he raised this case: A monk asked Master Madaishi, "Beyond the four propositions and transcending the hundred negations, I pray you, Master, point directly to the meaning of the Westward Coming.
Madaishi said, "I am weary today and cannot explain it for you; go ask Zhizang. The monk then asked Zhizang.
Cang said, "I have a headache today; I cannot explain this for you. You should ask my elder brother Hai. Hai said, "When I reach this point, I do not understand either.
The monk returned and reported this to Mazu. Mazu said, "Cang's head is white; Hai's head is black."

The Master picked up the case and said: "Master Ma was like one holding a charred *qingtong* lute, playing it with lingering grace. Yet how could he endure the two sons following behind, pointing their fingers and pressing the frets?
It was more than just water washing over a hundred rapids or the wind whistling through ten thousand gorges. Alas, those guests in the assembly failed to distinguish the *gong* and *shang* notes;
instead, they abruptly shifted the mode. But tell me, what mode did they shift to? If you do not yet know the subtlety within the lute..."
Merely listening to the sounds upon the strings.
Opening the furnace and ascending the hall: the monastic groves have grown cold and desolate; it is no different from these present times.

Although the veteran masters of all quarters may roast a few pieces of dead firewood, each warming their own doorsteps, yet they merely pick here and there, poke east and west, striking horizontally and blowing vertically.
"Bring together what belongs to your own house; all at once, blacken it out. Here in my place, I ask not whether things are large or small, dry or wet;
gather them all and heap them into the furnace. With but a spark of fire, bury them deep.

Wait for the time when they arrive of their own accord. "O Great Assembly! The time has arrived! [The Master] makes the gesture of fanning the fire with his whisk and cries: "Ha! The smoke and flames press upon you!"
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following case: A monk asked Yunmen, "If one kills father and mother, one repents before the Buddha;

but where does one repent for killing the Buddhas and the Patriarchs? Yunmen said, "Exposed. The Master composed this verse: Sweeping away the dust of the borders requires no toil; He breaks his bow in play to shoot at the azure sky.
Though he reaches out with all his might, he finds no strength; Who would have known that, with a mere flick of the hand, a hawk has fallen?
Ascending the hall on the anniversary of the Sage’s birthday: he rolls the Xuefeng ball and beats the Heshan drum; the lamp-stand and the lantern dance together.
This draws forth old Fenggan, who rides backward upon the tiger of the South Mountain. Why is this so? "When the Sage acts, all things behold."
Ascending the hall on the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month: Old Śākyamuni did not abide by his proper lot;

at midnight he fled into the Snow Mountains, freezing until his mouth was twisted and starving until his eyes turned white. Utterly without reason or understanding, he suddenly exclaimed, "How marvelous!

From that point on, he uttered颠言怪語 (eccentric and strange words), causing a commotion throughout heaven and earth. Amidst this vast clamor and noise, he deceived and led a host of people down into the cycle of rebirth.

To call a horse a donkey where it stands, and to point south as north—this "little boy of Guoqing," though he lives in another's house, wears another's clothes, and eats another's rice, insists on speaking of his faults. But tell me, what fault is there? Looking up at the sky, he laughs and says:
"It is very much like the father stealing the sheep and the son corroborating it."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient case: A monk once asked Caoshan, "When snow covers the thousand mountains, why is the solitary peak not white?
Caoshan replied, "You must know there is that which is 'extraordinary within the extraordinary. The monk asked, "What is this 'extraordinary within the extraordinary'?

Caoshan said, "It does not fall within the colors of the myriad mountains. The Master commented: "He concealed his mechanisms and laid a trap; even a single question was no easy matter. When that monk turned his head," [Caoshan struck him.]
Furthermore, Luojiaoshan fell into the overturned cart net. Guoqing’s critique was like this; yet where does it serve as an eye for people?
[The Master] took up his staff, struck it once on the ground, gave a shout, and descended from the seat.
When Master Jianweng arrived, he ascended the hall and said: "We have all traveled afar; we have all been on pilgrimage.
Who would have known that, in the end, we failed to recognize people? We have all been stirred up by him until our ears ring and our heads turn white with vexation.
Our resentment remains to this day, with nowhere to be placed—nowhere to be placed! He raised his whisk and said: "In my hand, I hold this broken wooden ladle."
Ascending the hall at the commencement of the summer retreat: Before the fifteenth day, the black-faced Persian kicks the moon;
after the fifteenth day, the long-bearded Earth-Constellation (Rāhu) grasps the wind in his hand. On the very fifteenth day, this old tree-dwelling mountain monk produces a dry excrement-stick;
he issues a decree to govern one hundred and eighty-seven iron pellets, from the eastern corridor to the western house.
Down! The floor is black lacquered according to the Vinaya; you must by no means touch it.

To thank the head officers for holding the whisk and ascending the hall: with a basket of grass for a drumstick and an earthen drum, those who have washed away their impurities will alone distinguish the true sound.

With the primal wine and the great soup, only the simple-minded will finally know the true flavor. There are a certain kind of fellows who, upon hearing this, say, "I have not yet even dipped my finger in it."
The true flavor is already known; one does not strain the ears. The correct sound is already distinguished; silence! The pure wind has been lost.
Ascending the hall, Yunmen addressed the assembly, saying: "On level ground there are countless dead people. To pass through the thorn-brake forest is to be a masterful hand.
A monk stepped forward and said, "If that is so, then the first seat in the hall must have some excellence. Yunmen said, "Su."
*Lu su lu*. The Master’s verse says: "The General’s command issued, the banners flash; The barbarian cavalry, in their confusion, lose all their might.
Though there may be those who suddenly gallop with great skill, They do not realize their bodies have already fallen into a heavy encirclement."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "To establish knowledge within seeing is the very root of ignorance. Three monkeys have been thrown down;

they prostrate before the Mountain King, who then distinguishes their ranks according to seniority—eight blows for one, thirteen for another—a uniform administration of discipline. To have no seeing within seeing..."
This is precisely nirvana. The sweet melon falls to the ground; the bitter gourd climbs the trellis. The garden deity reproaches them, saying:
"You should maintain your own station. Should you even slightly fail to follow the season, there shall be a blade to slay you, and a cauldron to boil you.

The Mountain said, "It is already here on the mountain; how can you take it away? He placed it on the ground and asked, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand.
The Mountain said, "I want to burn it. The Master [Zhaozhou] commented: "Old man Dongshan is preparing his own firewood.
When he runs into someone, there is immediately a matter of right and wrong. If that monk had seen him place the firewood on the ground and asked, 'Do you understand? he should have simply said..."
The Way, Master, is not easy. Even with a divine head and a demonic face, one could never accomplish it.
