The Mountain Gate: there is a gate and a path. Whether you people go east or west, if Xingjìngcí suddenly seizes you by the hand and cuts you off, where else will you find a foothold? He lets out a shout.
The Abbot [held] the staff horizontally and said, "In this way, in this way. He held the staff vertically and said, "Not in this way, not in this way.
He struck the ground with the staff and said, "How will you pass through this very barrier? Ho! Ho!"

He ascended the seat, offered incense to pray for the Emperor, and concluded the exchange of questions and answers. He then said: "The mountains of Eastern Zhejiang and the waters of Western Zhejiang—before a word is spoken, they have been pierced through; it lies right at the tips of one's toes."
The moon over the Southland; the clouds over the Northland. Parted beneath these words, they do not leave the range of one’s vision.
This old, tangled skein—something that the veteran masters of all quarters have been unable to pick up or handle—has now fallen into the hands of the new Jingci.
He drags it here and pulls it there, tripping up the monks of the world, each and every one of them, until they are leveled.
"Swallowing the Buddhas and Patriarchs"—then one sees the imperial wind fanning everywhere and the sun of grace shining once more. Auspicious vapors gather at the Dragon Pavilion;
purple mists coalesce at the Phoenix Gate. At such a time as this, where ultimately does the merit reside? After a long silence, he said: "The entire nation knows."
To cite another instance: when the founding patriarch Yongming first visited Fayan, he asked, "Aside from what you have been requesting instruction on, what sutra are you studying?
Yongming replied, "The *Avataṃsaka*. Fayan asked, "Under which category do the six aspects—totality, particularity, sameness, difference, formation, and disintegration—fall?
Yongming replied, "All phenomena, both mundane and supramundane, are fully endowed with these six aspects. Fayan then asked, "Does emptiness also possess the six aspects?"
"No," said Ming, "emptiness has no counterpart. Yan asked, "Why do you not ask me? Ming then asked, "Does emptiness possess the six characteristics?
Yan said, "Emptiness. At this, Ming attained enlightenment. Yan asked, "How do you understand this? Ming said, "Emptiness. Yan approved.
The Master’s verse says: "Empty, empty indeed, with neither front nor back; Picked up, it suddenly becomes two pieces.
Laid down at the corner of South Screen Mountain, For ten thousand ages, few have seen it. Do you wish to see it? [He strikes a circular shape with his whisk. "
The golden crow flies up onto the lapis lazuli hall.

That evening, during the informal sermon (xiaochan), the shadows of the screens are cast in soft relief; the silhouette of the stupa is tiered and sharp; the mountain colors are hazy and indistinct; and the lake’s surface glistens and ripples.
What a marvelous place for the Yellow-Faced Old Man to exercise his supernatural powers two thousand years ago!
Why should we not all lend a hand to raise up the great banner of radiant light and establish a new Dharma community? You three hundred or two hundred barefooted fellows—how can you sit idly by?
Each of you must take on your respective duties and positions, carry water and haul wood, and extensively provide offerings. Since this is so:
Furthermore, the new Elder has arrived; how shall we provide for him with a final banquet? [The Master] raises his whisk and says: "As the whisk sweeps the stone, the clouds follow the broom;
as the tea is brewed, the moon enters the cauldron. He then cites Xuefeng, who addressed the assembly, saying:
"On South Mountain there is a turtle-nosed snake. You all must watch it closely! It is a kind of evil creature, yet among them, it is somewhat superior."
Zi said, "In the hall today, there are many who have lost their lives.
Already fearful and shrinking back, Yunmen took his staff and brandished it before Xuefeng, making a gesture of intimidation. He had already struck him once.
Hearing this, Xuansha said, "What is the use of the Southern Mountains? *Du!* This basket-staff! With his staff, he drew a line across.
He said, "At one time, they were all lined up below. Do you still know where Xing Jìngcí stands? He threw down his staff and said, "Yayaya.
The following day, he ascended the seat and offered incense, respectfully making offerings on behalf of the late Emperor Huizong.
To provide spiritual sustenance for him...
"Your Sacred Majesty," he said, "Since the laying down of arms, we have beheld an era of Great Peace; you rode the dragon into the immortals' realm, leaving the colored clouds light behind.
In gratitude, there is only the water of West Lake, whose clear waves every night reflect the bright moon."
I request the Master of Transformations to ascend the hall. On South Mountain there is a multitude as numerous as counting sticks; they are all enemies and rivals of the Buddhas and Patriarchs.

With provisions for this summer retreat still so meager, how can we sit idly by without a plan? Within the city of Chang’an, at the head of the Fragrant Grass Ferry, we rely upon a master practitioner to seek on our behalf.
We must ensure that every single one is fully satiated and at ease. Suddenly, one encounters Vimalakīrti’s dwelling.
"Scholar! Pointing east, pointing west—how will you respond? Once a single word is scrutinized and penetrated, the old Ox King is made to laugh.
He ascended the hall because of this matter: "The Buddha-dharma in a village of three households cannot be employed at the crossroads; if it were to be employed there,"
Gold does not trade with gold. The Buddha-dharma at the crossroads is of no use in a village of three houses.
If it were used there, water would not wash water. When used, it is not used; when employed, it is not employed. Set this aside for a moment: what, then, is the Buddha-dharma?
The two masters of the Southern Mountain established the Righteous Meaning (Saddharmanirdeśa) to subdue the demonic hordes; yet their debate has not yet reached a conclusion.
Victory or defeat! Master Yuling of the State of Yan then challenged the *tongshi sheren* (attendant official).
With a single pull at the source, the crimson banner fluttered into his own hands. He struck the meditation seat and descended from it.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an anecdote: A monk asked Chan Master Furi Bi, “What is the Seal of Vairocana?
Bi replied, “A straw sandal treading through snow. The monk said, “I do not understand. Bi said, “Every step leaves its trace. The Master commented:
“It is like an insect gnawing through wood; by chance, it forms patterns. Furi indeed attained the subtle essence, yet he was simply unable to bring this monk to life.”
He suddenly asked Jingci, "What is the Vairocana Seal? Jingci held up one hand. The student did not understand;
Jingci then slapped him across the cheek. Was he saved by this? Or was he not saved?

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "One cannot seek it with a mind of intention—this is like a fish swallowing a straight hook. One cannot attain it with a mind of non-intention—this is like a dog gnawing at a stone.
One cannot construct it through words and speech—this is like a pigeon devouring a live hawk. One cannot penetrate it through silent stillness—this is like a rat biting a tiger.
These four turning-words involve both life and death, and both release and gathering. You all, one by one...
I understand; I grant you that there is a place of peace and ease within the four modes of deportment.
However, if you do not know this, five days from now someone will question you, and you must not end up like Master Chen of Xianlin Monastery, shaking his bell and pestle while chanting "Māṇi Māṇi."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised up Dongshan’s address to the assembly, which said: "You must know that there is a matter above the Buddha.
A monk asked, "What is the matter above the Buddha? Dongshan replied, "Not a Buddha. Yunmen commented: "It cannot be named; it cannot be described.
That is why he says 'not. The Master commented: "There is sinew in his eyes and bone in his tongue; with all one's strength, one can only manage to say 'not'."
The Buddha cannot be named; his form cannot be grasped. He is truly like Wang Xiaobo’s two worn-out straw sandals.
Entering the hall, he raised the case of Chan Master Daguan Ying, who addressed the assembly, saying: "The seven Buddhas are the subjects of nature; the myriad dharmas are the slaves of the mind.
Now tell me, where is the master? He then shouted himself and said: "All those from the seven Buddhas downward have now shown their heads! Furthermore—

[The Master] himself responded with "Yes. [The assembly] each waited respectfully. The Master commented: "To call the Seven Buddhas 'subordinates of nature' and to point to the myriad dharmas as 'slaves of the mind'—Daguan claims for himself that he has a way to transcend this.
Yet, when he himself shouts and himself responds with 'Yes,' this is still merely the business of slaves and subordinates.
When has the true master ever been seen even in a dream? Do you all wish to see him? With his whisk, he swept once.
Wiping away the clouds: at dawn, a breeze of spring stirs, causing the hundred varieties of flowers throughout the gardens to bloom.
Holding his bowl, he arrived at Wanshou Monastery in Pingjiang and requested a *xiaocan* (informal discourse). "For thirty years, my straw sandals have been tightly bound;

only where the peach blossoms bloom does one first recognize the path. Six or seven meditation cushions have been worn through; only when the bamboo curtain is rolled up does one truly see the world."

To give these two lacquered buckets thirty blows would be appropriate; for they do not realize that the moment one is born with a single "gup" cry, the great matter of studying Zen is already complete.

Such talk could only be possible at the side of the Gusu Terrace, before the Hall of Right Reception, where the Old Monk of Direct Pointing and Single Transmission sits in morning and evening *zana* with the monks from the two mountains.
Regarding the division of deliberation: if one is a "fox of the city" or a "rat of the shrine," a wild duck of the marsh or a crow of the forest, where else would one go to peck and feed?
Jìngcí’s matching and his elevating and suppressing are much like thrusting a spade into a rice basket or stirring a ladle in a water jar;
they make Hán Dàbó of old fall over with laughter. Again, he raised the case: Púxián Bǎopū passed on a message to Sīdà, saying, "Why do you not..."
Descending the mountain to teach and transform sentient beings, Dayun said: "The Buddhas of the three periods of time have all been swallowed by me in a single mouth;
where else could there be any sentient beings left to transform? The Master (Zhaozhou) took up the case and said: "Baogong sells his wares with a sharp edge; Sita feigns craftiness.
Who would have known that this struck upon the matter in the heart of Jingci? Since I came down from the mountain forty days ago, there has likewise been no sentient being to transform."
There are no Buddhas to be swallowed either. But tell me, what has been accomplished? After a long silence, he said: "A colander without a handle strains the spring breeze;
it stirs the falling petals until they fly one by one."

At Jiaoshan Temple in Zhenjiang Prefecture, he was requested to give a small-scale discourse (*xiaocan*). The profound mysteries of the Buddha-dharma are displayed according to circumstances even in the middle of the marketplace;
the essential subtleties of the Way of Chan are implemented as the occasion arises even in a village of three households. Suddenly, a gust of black wind blows without cause.

Upon arriving at the kingdom of Haimen, he encountered a wicked spiritual friend who bites pigs and dogs. This one has opened a great furnace and wielded great tongs and hammers to smelt and forge the great-minded patch-robed monks.
The Buddha-dharma and Chan Way of the Southern Mountains have been squeezed into a single lump and cast into the heart of the Yangtze River.
Why is this so? At Jinshan Temple, the mountain envelops the temple; at Jiaoshan, the mountain envelops the temple. Thousands and tens of thousands of people...
The title: It is simply this very matter. [He] strikes the sounding block once with his staff. He then cites: Linji asked the Hall Master, "Where have you come from?
The Master said, "I have come from selling yellow rice in the prefectural city. Linji said, "Have you sold it all? The Master said, "I have sold it all.
Linji took his staff, drew a line across it, and said, "Can you sell this too? The Master then shouted. Linji then...
He struck him. Later, when the head cook arrived, Linji brought up the previous conversation. The cook said, "The Abbot did not understand your meaning. Linji asked, "And what about you?
The cook then bowed, and Linji struck him as well. The Master (Zhaozhou) commented:
"Linji had a fine staff, but it is a pity he only managed to strike two lacquer buckets. Had he struck one [of the right kind] at that time, I—"

"I have not even had a meal from this group. Carrying my bowl, I shall return. In the intercalary fourth month, the summer retreat began. During the small assembly (xiaocan), he said: "I traveled once through the South, yet I never encountered a master who could truly strike the staff and penetrate the Dharma.
He was a man who could outwit others and bring them to their end. I traveled three thousand li, sold my bedding, and came here specifically for his sake."
This matter has come about through such causes and conditions. To kill people out of shame and fear—there are many like this even under the gate of Pure Compassion.
For now, let us shorten the long term into a short term, and consolidate three sessions into one. Let us try to test them from the very beginning by pricking them with needles.
If they were to die at a single prick or revive at a single poke, I, the old monk, would not fail to burn fine incense as an offering.
What does this mean? Every three years there is one intercalary month; every four months the moon appears full again.
Again, Zhenjing addressed the assembly, saying: "Today is the second fourth month. Have you not heard the ancients say, 'To let pass one move is to fall into the second'?
Although it is the second, it remains simply the beginning of summer, gradually growing hot. A-he-he! There is [a reality]."

Profit and loss; he does not refrain from frequenting the marketplace. The "Leakage Basket" of Chengdu in Western Sichuan—three or two copper coins scattered before everyone’s eyes, each capable of curing an illness. Yet no one knows the price of rice in Luling.
The Master picked it up and said: "Everyone, this old, stagnant stock has been cast away within the monastic community for some time."
Someone was peering with their eyes [at it], and Jingci simply pulled it over with his hand; he used it exactly as required. How marvelous! How marvelous!

As the early summer heat gradually increases, five days ago in the front hall, before a word had even been spoken, I had already said it all. You sleepyheads, you naturally conceal it right in your own faces.
How rare! How rare! The broken basket from Chengdu Prefecture in Western Sichuan has been refurbished by the rear hall.
He brought it forth: "To bring all people to life takes not even half a dose.
As for the price of Luling rice—wait until everyone has eaten, and I will discuss it with you from within your nostrils. He gave a shout and descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised this case: A monk asked Dongshan, "When cold and heat arrive, how can one avoid them?
Dongshan said, "Why not go to a place where there is no cold or heat to avoid them? The monk asked, "What is the place where there is no cold or heat?
Dongshan said, "In the cold, it will freeze you to death; in the heat, it will scorch you to death. The Master commented: "To cast one's body across within cold and heat—cold and heat..."
With his hands hanging down at his sides, Dongshan considered himself a master; yet he did not realize that the "single-word barrier" upon his own tongue had been pierced through by this monk.
Entering the hall, he said: "I, this mountain monk, have a phrase that resides within each of you, level and even. You all..."

A single phrase. From the perspective of this mountain monk, it is full of twists and turns. [The Master] then raised his whisk and said: "Brought over by the left hand, it was originally but a single staff;
lifted up by the right hand, it is not two different things. Why then, from the corner of the bed, does he cast it directly in front of one's face?
Five pairs, ten items—when you try to take them, you cannot; when you try to let them go, it is difficult. After a long silence, he said: "Difficult, difficult!"
Small Assembly for the End of the Summer Retreat. In these one hundred and twenty days of summer retreat, there is a fine saying:
before the winnowing basket moves its lips, the broom has already revealed its intent. Have you not seen it? When Guishan asked Yangshan, "Ji-zi, during this summer, what were your duties down below?
Yangshan replied, "I cleared a patch of fallow land and sowed a basketful of seed. This is it.
Tianju Nu. Guishan said, "This summer you have not spent it in vain; you have settled your breath according to the source.
Yangshan looked up and asked, "What did the Master do this summer? Looking upward, Guishan said, "One meal at midday, one sleep after nightfall, and nothing but coarse flour gruel and fruit.
Yangshan said, "The Master, too, has not spent this summer in vain. [Yangshan] crossed his arms behind his back.
Handan bowed his head in understanding and then stuck out his tongue. The wildcat bit its own tail. Guishan said, "Jizi, why do you injure your own life? It cannot be saved.
The family style of Guishan and Handan has already been witnessed by everyone; now tell me, what about the assembly at Jingci?
Sharing a bed and huddling heads together to sleep, each opens their eyes and dreams; is this empty passing, or is it not empty passing?
Striking the whisk, he says: "The twin banners withdraw the lightning flash; a single sword leans against the cold heavens. Again he cites: An ancient worthy said, "Mind is not Buddha;
wisdom is not the Way. The Master offers a verse: "The moon shines upon the white wall, even whiter; the candle enters..."
Even more crimson within the gauze-like clouds. At night’s chill, one hears fallen leaves by the well; already startled that autumn colors have reached the *wutong* trees.
Ascending the hall: Before the fifteenth day, it is bound but not yet released. After the fifteenth day, it is released but no longer bound.
On this very day, let go of binding; let go of releasing. The straw sandals face the cheeks with eight ears protruding; the staff lies across the body, providing support.
At both ends, monks from the five lakes and four seas become enemies.
Ascending the hall, he raised the following case: One day, when a monk came to visit him, Guishan rose from his seat. The monk said, "Please do not rise, Reverend.
Guishan said, "This old monk has never sat down. The monk said, "I have never bowed. Guishan said, "How can there be no [bowing]?"
Li: The Master picked it up and said, "Those who rush up the mountain do not know its height; those who wade through the water in confusion do not perceive its depth.
Because of this, the family way has been eroded day by day and month by month. Then, picking up his staff, he said, "If Guishan had known of this earlier...
After a long silence, he said, "When one has money, one buys gold."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Yellow leaves fall before the courtyard; white clouds gather upon the ridge. There is not much to this flavor—what person can discourse with me?
Suddenly, someone comes forward and seizes him, saying, "In your own house, you have a livelihood as vast as heaven.
Why do you put on such an air of poverty and speak such cold, insipid words? He then lets out a great laugh and says: [The Chan master laughs heartily.]
"Only the Spring and Autumn Annals can truly know me.

On the occasion of the Mid-Autumn Festival, he ascended the hall: "Whenever one encounters the Mid-Autumn Festival, everyone vies to admire the Mid-Autumn moon. Pointing at it, they point; gazing at it, they gaze."
Speaking of the bottom, speaking of the bottom—when has it ever been apart from fullness and deficiency? Only old Changsha loved him; with one kick, he toppled little Śākyamuni.
Radiant and brilliant, utterly beyond all restriction—no one knows for certain whose house it has fallen into.
The posthumous letter from Master Beilin of Leifeng arrived. He ascended the hall and said: "A single gust of western wind / Has leveled Beilin in an instant.
/ The morning apes and night cranes / Wander in empty lamentation. / Alas! Alas! / The light of his precepts still shines upon the high terrace."

Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the case of Jia Shan and Ding Shan. While the two were traveling together and conversing, Ding Shan said, "If there is no Buddha within birth and death, then there is no birth and death.
Jia Shan said, "If there is a Buddha within birth and death, then one does not become deluded by birth and death.
The two could not agree on who was right or wrong, so they went together to see Da Mei and asked him, "We do not know which of these two men's views is correct."
“Which one is closer? Daiman said, “One is close, the other is distant. Jakuan asked, “Which one is close?
Daiman said, “Go away for now; come back tomorrow. The next day Jakuan asked again. Daiman said, “He who is close does not ask; he who asks is not close.
After Jakuan established his own monastery, he said, “At that time, when I was with Daiman, I lost an eye. The Master commented: “One person...”
Golden needles and embroidered brocade; a single person with jade thread gathers the flowered curtain. Both are brought forth through the skill of ingenious craftsmanship.
Before Damei, turning it over and back again, its radiance grows ever more brilliant. Do you know where Jia Shan applied his final stroke?
Unfurling it and hanging it high upon the wild hall, the hundred birds take flight in alarm, not daring to cry out.
Ascending the hall, he said: "A single Mount Sumeru is lifted onto one's head without knowing its weight; a half-inch of lamp-wick grass is hidden in one's hand without knowing its lightness.

Those who act in such a manner may be called fools, may be called deluded, may be called lacking self-reflection, and may be called devoid of standard. Nevertheless—" with these words, he struck once with his staff and said: "Arrived!"
When it was not yet time for the formal session, there was still sound [of voices].
He ascended the hall and, citing the occasion when Han Yu and the Master of the *Zhao Lun* were drinking tea, Han Yu asked: "I have heard that you can lecture on the *Zhao Lun*;
is this true? The Master replied: "I dare not say so. Han Yu said: "In the treatise, there is the principle of 'the non-transmigration of things'; is this correct? The Master replied: "It is."
The Master knocked the cup down and said, "What is the meaning of this? The host was speechless.
The Master remarked, "Master Zhao Lun of Han Wen Gong, even drinking tea you do not act according to your own nature.
The principle of 'Non-Transmigration of Things' is indeed impossible to clarify. Alas! What a waste of a single cup!"

Ascending the hall on the occasion of the Sage’s Birthday: The stream flows with the reflection of the rainbow; the pivot revolves with the flash of lightning. A Sage has appeared, and his transformation permeates all distant lands.
How shall one proclaim a single phrase of auspicious praise for the Southern Mountain? With palms joined and heads bowed, he says: *Namo Yan-shou Wang* (Homage to the King of Extended Life).
*Namo Chang-shou Wang* (Homage to the King of Longevity).
Ascending the hall, he raised the case of Xuefeng showing the assembly: "Sitting by the side of a rice basket, a man starved to death; facing a river, a man thirsting to death.
'Zenglang! Zenglang! Thirty years ago, I too came this way. Xuansha said, "Sitting inside the rice basket."
A man who dies of hunger; a man submerged up to his head in water, dying of thirst. This is precisely the confession made before one has yet crossed the mountain pass.
Yunmen said, "The whole body is food; the whole body is water. *Pfft!* This lame fellow! Pushing the door with a shove, he breaks his own leg. Is it food? Is it water?
Under the gate of Jingci, these men who die of hunger and men who die of thirst need not even be mentioned for now.
In the ordinary course of eating and drinking, chew thoroughly and swallow whole as you please; however, do not forget the source from which you come.
[The Master] requested that the abbot ascend the hall for a formal discourse. The abbot raised up his staff and addressed the assembly, saying:
"If you have a staff, I will give you my staff; if you have no staff, I will take yours away. The Master commented: "Presence and absence."
A knot grows upon a branch; a branch grows upon a knot. These are equally the master’s staffs for play. The old *bājiǎo* (plantain tree) enjoys the advantage.
Nanshan, not begrudging his effort, reaches out to uphold them. Handing over the master’s staff, he calls the attendant and says:
"The Office of Construction has no staffs to use; borrow these for the time being."
The Buddha ascends the hall for his *nirvāṇa* discourse: The sun is warm, spraying the courtyard flowers; the breeze is light, swaying the willows by the bank.
The old barbarian enters extinction at the Twin Trees, yet to this day he still bares his chest.
One or two of you—if you can see through this—may then perpetuate the radiance of ten thousand ages. If it is otherwise, I shall blind your eyes and silence my mouth.

Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised up the case of Zhaozhou. Once, when a monk was taking his leave, Zhaozhou asked, "Where are you going? The monk replied, "I am going to study the Buddha-dharma in various quarters.
Zhaozhou held up his whisk and said, "Do not stay where there is a Buddha; pass quickly through where there is no Buddha.
When you encounter people three thousand miles away, do not speak of this mistakenly. The monk said, "If that is so, then I shall not go. Zhaozhou said, "Pluck it out!"
"Picking willow flowers, picking willow flowers. The Master’s verse says: "Emerging from waves a thousand fathoms deep, extending a hand before a cliff ten thousand cubits high.
An old man of seven hundred years of age, stubbornly puts on a display of ugliness. Picking willow flowers, picking willow flowers;
he turns his body and leaps onto a tree, startling the crows from the evening woods."
Offering incense on the anniversary of the passing of Master Fojian, he held up the incense and said: "This very thing is what subjects one's ancestors to slow torture;

this very thing is what brings calamity upon one's descendants. On the eighteenth day of the third month, to emerge from the womb of a donkey and enter the belly of a horse—this too is that very thing.
O-yang! O-yang! He then inserted the incense and said: "Not only do I repay you with this, I also wish to humiliate you with it."
Ascending the hall, he thundered the Dharma-thunder and struck the Dharma-drum; he spread the clouds of compassion and sprinkled the nectar of immortality.
Master Yongjia was originally a dragon within stagnant waters; this mountain monk cannot but rely upon his spiritual power. Behold him galloping and transforming upon level ground!
He gave a shout and said, "The Dharma-thunder has thundered! Striking the meditation seat, he said, "The Dharma-drum has been struck! With these words, he descended from the seat.
He sweeps with his whisk and says, "The clouds of compassion are spreading. He sprinkles with his whisk and says, "The nectar of immortality is being showered down.
Thus, the mountains, rivers, the great earth, the grasses, trees, and forests all flourish and all grow lush and verdant.
But tell me, does this rotten tangle within Xujia Garden still have this message? Raising his whisk and looking around, he says, "The sprouts have grown!"
A Small Sermon for the Summer Retreat. [The Master] raises his staff and says: "Aha! Aha! Under the bright sun and clear sky, there is such a matter.
This staff suddenly appears as the head for all of you. For these ninety days of the summer retreat, you wish to stay but cannot stay;
you wish to go but cannot go. You are like a dog fallen into water, like a sheep caught in a fence, like a monkey trapped in a cage, and like a tiger fallen into a pit."
At this moment, does the old man dwelling in the mountains have no skillful means? It must be that the mind itself consents and the head itself nods.
The Master of the Staff joyfully opens the eyes for all people; he strikes once and says, "A-ha-ha!
Under the blue sky and bright sun, there is no such thing. He further cites: Xuansha asked Jingqing, "Not seeing a single dharma is the Great..."
"Faults and afflictions. [The Master] asked, "Tell me, which dharma is this? Jingqing pointed at a pillar and said, "Is it not that you do not see this very dharma?
Xuefeng said, "As for the clear water and white rice of Zhejiang, you may eat as much as you like; but as for the Buddha-dharma, it is not yet there.
The Master commented: "Xuefeng’s tongue was like a blade; Jingqing’s finger was like an arrow. In their laughter and talk, each displayed their strategic wits. To act—

What kind of face does this man have? Why? Have you not heard it said that when he ascended the hall at Zhangquan Fujian, it was like the earth supporting a mountain—unaware of the mountain’s towering loftiness; his sharp edges were revealed, like a stone containing jade.
One does not know that jade is without flaw until its luster and patterns are manifest. If one can be thus, this is true renunciation. HŪṂ. It is just like this;
yet if you wish to enter the gate of Jingci Monastery, the West Lake still stands between you.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following case: A monk asked Zhimen, "What is it like when the lotus flower has not yet emerged from the water?

Zhimen said, "The lotus flower. The monk asked, "What is it like after it has emerged? Zhimen said, "The lotus leaf. The Master composed this verse: "Delicate jade mooring lines spread across the tender sprouts;
Fragrant buds cluster upon the fresh leaves. What secret mechanism does the Creator hold? He rends open his belly and pours out his heart."
[The Master] leaked [the secret]. He ascended the hall and cited a monk’s question to Dongshan: “What is the Buddha? Dongshan replied, “Three catties of hemp. The Master commented:
“Old Dongshan took his three-inch blade and severed the life-roots of the monks of the world. Although hundreds of years have passed...”
The year [is such that] its sharp edge is chillingly keen. Today at Jingci, I shall give you a direct lift—blood dripping drop by drop.
On the first day of the eighth month, he ascended the hall and said: "Beside the white artemisia isles, at the head of the red dogwood banks, the fisherman finds his joy and nudges his solitary boat.
A flight of wild geese, two rows in length, takes flight; seven or eight sand gulls scatter across the waves. The fishing line remains..."
The hand follows, releasing and gathering as it may. At that time, a golden-scaled fish bites the straight hook.
On the Mid-Autumn Festival, he ascends the hall to express his gratitude to Baizhang and Xitang. He cites the occasion when Mazu, along with Xitang, Baizhang, and Nanquan were admiring the moon.
Mazu asked, "At this very moment, what is it? Xitang said, "It is precisely right for making offerings. Baizhang said:
"Exactly right for cultivation. Nanquan shook his sleeves and departed. Mazu said, "The Sūtras return to the archives; Zen returns to the sea.
Only Puyan alone transcends the mundane world. The Master [Zhaozhou] commented: "Xitang’s offerings were light enough to tip the scale; Baizhang’s cultivation fell short by an inch.
When Nanquan shook his sleeves and left, the straw dog chased the iron ox. Fortunately for Master Ma..."
Flat as a mirror—why must it be curved like a hook?
On the Ninth Day of the Ninth Month, ascending the hall: the ninth day of the ninth month. A single phrase possesses a standard and a measure;
it has no handle. Only Tao Jingjie knows the seams and cracks: "Tranquil, he gazes upon the Southern Mountains; laughing and swaggering beneath the eastern hedge."

Drawing lots to solicit alms. Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said: "To cease contemplation while lost in the source, or to sweep away dust while remaining ignorant of oneself—how many monks are trapped here!
At Jingci, I cannot help but take the head as the tail and the tail as the head. The three fellows in the hall shall serve as my temporary slaves;
the five hundred honored ones in the sanctuary shall act as my momentary attendants. With all our might, let us rouse ourselves!"
The ancient family tradition: First, we pray for the longevity of the One Man; second, we forge the peace of the Six Armies; third, we wish for the joy of the myriad people.
Only then do we open the Gate of Heaven and unbar the Door of Earth, so that every single person upon the Chang’an market may know that the alms bowl has no bottom.
Raising his staff, he says: “Casually obtaining one tally as I return. He strikes the table once and says: “How thoroughly you are satisfied!”
"Kill you quickly! [The Master] ascends the hall.
He cites a monk who asked Yunmen, "If one does not give rise to a single thought, is there still any transgression? Yunmen said, "Mount Sumeru. The Master comments:
"The lake’s light is deep and clear; the wild colors are hazy and vast. An old man in a straw raincoat and bamboo hat is deeply immersed in a state of weary repose."
Fishing. Suddenly, one encounters it; turning the oars and shifting the raft, one immediately beholds snow-white waves a thousand fathoms deep and billowing clouds ten thousand layers thick.
At the small assembly for the Winter Solstice—Spring Equinox, Autumn Equinox, Summer Solstice, and Winter Solstice—the heavens and earth revolve in a cycle. Raising the master’s staff, he said:
This is the One Qi (Single Vital Energy). A-he-he! The Master’s staff of Jingci Monastery is stiff and rigid, dark and vast;

it transcends yin and yang and dwells neither in cold nor heat. It opens the eyes of Śākyamuni and brandishes them in the dead of night; it knocks out the teeth of Bodhidharma and pulls them out after nine years of entanglement.
It seizes the very life-force of all the monks under heaven with a single pinch, making them seek death yet unable to find it.

He has met death; though he seeks life, he cannot find it. Why, then, did he arrive on the eighteenth day of the eleventh month in the sixth year of Baoyu, while sitting here upon this counting seat, to preemptively extend his hand and bare his feet? He struck the sounding block and said: "Master Monk Zhigong."
Again, it is recounted: Dongshan and his senior teacher Mi went to a bakery. Mi drew a circle on the ground and said, "Take this away.
Dongshan said, "Bring it here. Mi then desisted. The Master [Zhaozhou] commented: "He would not take it away; he could not bring it here.
These two fellows were a pair of fools. To this day, they lie in disarray upon the level ground, covered by green moss."
Ascending the hall: Before the eighteenth day, the yang wanes and the yin waxes; after the eighteenth day, the yang waxes and the yin wanes.
On this very day, yin and yang meet and harmonize, their waxing and waning merging into one. Beneath the South Mountain stands a single tree of thousand-threaded cypress.
Intertwining branches and crisscrossing joints; weaving with the shuttle of the moon and the loom of the wind. One layer of emerald threads rises above another.

To the two halls’ masters who hold the whisk and the monastery’s administrators who prepare the offerings: Ascending the hall. There is the "one-flavor Chan," where the black-lacquered staff stands east and west, its head lacking and its tail incomplete.
There is the "five-flavors Chan," where the white porcelain bowl holds deep reserves yet serves shallow portions, lacking even a fraction of its full measure.
[The Master] took up half of his fan and struck a circular shape with it, saying: "It is all contained within the sleeves of Jingci; you must not move it."
One must not speak of this. Why? Frugality gives rise to unfiliality; righteousness emerges from years of plenty.

On New Year’s Eve, during the small session of instruction: The ox sleeping peacefully in the open field has not yet shed its golden tether; it remains ever within the gaze [of the owner], yet the cowherd finds it difficult to catch.
Now that the year is exhausted and the season at its end, one is certainly not like the old Fachang, burning pieces of firewood.
They perform the *Sōden-gaku* (village music) and act as objects of amusement for the assembly. Each person has their own head;

with two horns pointing to heaven and four hooves treading the earth, they go out to the lake in the morning and return to the mountain ridges in the evening. Lying across or rolling over, they all remain within the pens of the Southern Mountain.
It is simply that the herders do not know them and those who ride them do not recognize them. Does the great assembly wish to recognize them? [He] uses—
He brandishes his whisk in the manner of a whip and says, "Chit! He speaks again, saying, "Lao! [Hold fast to the end of the rope! He raises it once more.
A monk asked Master Kaixian Xian, "What is it like when the year has ended and the age is spent? Kaixian said, "As usual, it is still cold in the early spring."
The Master commented: "Kaixian could truly be said to have blown on the fire with the wind; he used little effort. Suddenly, someone asked about Jingci:
"When the year is exhausted and the age comes to an end, what then? [Jingci replied: "The winter ice is dispatched by a thousand chopsticks; the spring willow is summoned by a single thread."
Ascending the hall on the first day of the first month: Year after year is a good year; day after day is a good day. Today at South Mountain, the excellence is even more extraordinary than usual.
The stone man rises to bow and the great man makes a formal salutation. Why is it so? A snake grows horns; a tiger sprouts wings.
Ascending the hall at Huzhou, he said: "Smoke mists the trees on the bank; water submerges the sedges on the marsh.
At the ferryhead, the fishing boat is nudged; wild ducks fly past with graceful ease. Recalling Baizhang’s nostrils, they were pinched by Mazu;
even now, he still makes sounds of wincing in pain. For Jingci to speak thus is like throwing a stone into the air."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient case: A monk asked Mazu, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Mazu called to the monk to come forward;
as the monk approached, Mazu struck him with his palm and said, "Six ears do not share a secret. The Master commented: "Master Ma said..."
Come closer. It was already a conspiracy of six ears; how much more so when you strike another blow?
Yet, those who truly understand the Duke of Zhou’s creation of rites and music are few indeed.
At the Nirvana Assembly, he ascended the hall and said: "The World-Honored One, at the assembly for his parinirvāṇa, rubbed his chest with his hand and addressed the multitude:
'The illness that cannot be grasped has been revealed. He then said: 'You should carefully observe my body, which is the color of purple-polished gold.'"
Behold me with full satisfaction; let there be no cause for later regret. My words have not been few, nor have they been spoken in confusion or error.

Whether you say that I have entered parinirvāṇa, you are not my disciple; whether you say that I have not entered parinirvāṇa, you are likewise not my disciple. Even at the moment of death, I am still speaking of medical treatises.
At that time, the assembly of one million people all attained realization. "Hūṃ! Hūṃ! [I say: they were all merely leaning on fences and groping along walls.
If there were even one or half a person who could turn over their skin, Old Gautama would not have it even if he wanted to die.
Ascending the hall, he said: Clouds gather and the deep valley is still; the rain ceases and the secluded ravine resounds. The breeze is warm and the hidden birds sing;
the sun is bright and the secluded grasses turn green. The Second Patriarch did not understand, and his arm was severed. Guizong did not comprehend, and his two eyes were rubbed away.

This causes every patch-robed monk to be half-doubting and half-believing, half-intoxicated and half-awake; how could they know that from the very beginning, he has been filling his mouth, chewing the blossoms and savoring the essence?
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised an example, citing how Guishan addressed the assembly: "Traveling monks must sit amidst sounds and forms; you must lie down amidst sounds and forms.
Shushan stepped forward and asked, "What is the phrase that does not fall into sounds and forms? Guishan held up his whisk.
Shushan said, "This is still a phrase that falls into sounds and forms. Guishan then returned to his quarters. Not attaining realization, Shushan took his leave.
Xiangyan said, "Why do you not stay for a while? Shanshan said, "I have no affinity with the Master. Xiangyan said, "What circumstance prevents us from being in accord?
Shanshan then recounted the previous conversation. Xiangyan said, "I have a saying. Shanshan asked, "What is it?
Xiangyan said, "When words are uttered, they are not sound; before form appears, there is no object. Shanshan said, "So, it turns out there is someone here!"

"After my elder brother has departed, there is a place for me to stay, and I shall come to keep you company. Later that evening, when Guishan returned, he asked Yanguan, "Is the short *ācārya* still here?
Yanguan replied, "He has already left. Guishan asked, "What did you say to him? Yanguan said, "I also spoke to him.
Guishan said, "Try to quote what you said. Yanguan said, "'The utterance of words is not sound; before form, there is no object.'"
Miaoyan asked, "What did he say? Yan said, "He deeply approved of it. Miaoyan laughed and said, "I thought the dwarf had some merit;
it turns out he was just stuck right here. This fellow will have a dwelling place in the future: near the mountains, there will be no wood to burn;
near the water, there will be no water to drink. The Master [Zhaozhou] commented: "To support his head, Miaoyan used both hands and feet."
Lù supported its tail from the side; Xiāngyán emptied his very heart and liver [in his devotion], yet the attendants could not pull out the short-legged "uncle" from his sleeves.
